title: Gradient-flow scale setting from octet baryon masses in N$^3$LO covariant chiral perturbation theory
summary: We determine the gradient-flow scale $t_0$ by analyzing the lowest-lying octet-baryon masses on the Coordinated Lattice Simulations (CLS) $N_f=2+1$ ensembles in covariant baryon chiral perturbation theory up to next-to-next-to-next-to leading order (N$^3$LO). By including the finite-volume corrections self-consistently and the discretization effects from Symanzik effective field theory, we obtain a good description of the RQCD data and determine the gradient-flow scale to be $\sqrt{8t_{0,\mathrm{ph}}}=0.4120(14)_\mathrm{stat.}(16)_\mathrm{sys.}$ fm with sub-percent precision. The predicted octet baryon masses agree well with the experimental values in the isospin limit. Using the Feynman-Hellmann theorem, we also estimate the nucleon sigma terms, which are consistent with direct determinations from three-point correlation functions on the same CLS ensembles.

AI.tldr: This paper determines the gradient-flow scale $t_0$ using octet-baryon masses from CLS $N_f=2+1$ lattice QCD ensembles, employing covariant baryon chiral perturbation theory at N$^3$LO with self-consistent finite-volume and Symanzik discretization corrections; it achieves sub-percent precision for $\sqrt{8t_0}$ and validates predictions against experiment and nucleon sigma terms via the Feynman-Hellmann theorem.
AI.motivation: To precisely determine the gradient-flow scale $t_0$ — a key reference scale in lattice QCD — by leveraging baryonic observables and controlling systematic uncertainties including finite-volume and discretization effects.
AI.method: Covariant baryon chiral perturbation theory at N$^3$LO, augmented with self-consistent finite-volume corrections and Symanzik effective field theory for discretization effects; analysis applied to CLS $N_f=2+1$ lattice ensembles; nucleon sigma terms estimated via the Feynman-Hellmann theorem.
AI.result: $\sqrt{8t_{0,\mathrm{ph}}}=0.4120(14)_\mathrm{stat.}(16)_\mathrm{sys.}$ fm (sub-percent total uncertainty); excellent agreement of predicted octet-baryon masses with experimental isospin-limit values; Feynman-Hellmann–derived sigma terms consistent with direct three-point function extractions on same ensembles.
AI.conclusion: The gradient-flow scale $t_0$ can be robustly determined from baryon masses using high-order chiral effective theory with controlled systematics; this approach provides a precise, theoretically grounded calibration of the lattice scale and corroborates consistency between different hadronic observables and extraction methods.

title: Unfreezing topology using out-of-equilibrium replica exchanges
summary: Parallel Tempering on Boundary Conditions (PTBC) mitigates topological freezing by exchanging configurations between replicas that interpolate between periodic and open boundaries on a small defect. We generalize PTBC by replacing the instantaneous swap with a short out-of-equilibrium protocol, in which the defect couplings of two replicas are exchanged gradually while the fields around the defect are updated. We show that the swap rate depends only on the average work spent along the out-of-equilibrium trajectory by virtue of Crooks' and Jarzynski's fluctuation relations. From the theoretical derivation of the scaling of the work as a function of the number of replicas, protocol length, and defect size, we predict the swap rate and the optimal protocol length. These predictions are tested in the $2d$ $\mathrm{CP}^{N-1}$ model with $N=21$. The optimal setup agrees with the measured one, the total computational cost at fixed statistical precision decreases by $\gtrsim40\%$ with respect to standard PTBC for all explored lattice spacings, and the required number of replicas at fixed acceptance is halved.

AI.tldr: This paper generalizes Parallel Tempering on Boundary Conditions (PTBC) by replacing instantaneous swaps with gradual, out-of-equilibrium protocols for defect coupling exchange; using fluctuation theorems and scaling analysis, it predicts and validates optimal protocol parameters, achieving >40% reduction in computational cost and halving required replicas in the 2d CP^{N−1} model (N=21).
AI.motivation: To mitigate topological freezing in lattice field simulations more efficiently than standard PTBC, which suffers from low swap acceptance due to instantaneous boundary-condition swaps.
AI.method: Generalizes PTBC by implementing a finite-time, out-of-equilibrium protocol for exchanging defect couplings between replicas; leverages Crooks’ and Jarzynski’s fluctuation relations to express swap rate in terms of average dissipated work; derives analytical scaling of work with replica count, protocol duration, and defect size to predict optimal protocol length and swap rate.
AI.result: Analytical predictions for swap rate and optimal protocol length match numerical measurements in the 2d CP^{N−1} model (N=21); total computational cost at fixed statistical precision improves by ≥40% over standard PTBC across all tested lattice spacings; number of replicas needed for fixed swap acceptance is reduced by 50%.
AI.conclusion: Gradual, work-controlled boundary-condition interpolation significantly enhances sampling efficiency in topologically constrained systems; fluctuation-theorem-based protocol design provides a principled, predictive framework for optimizing parallel tempering schemes beyond conventional instantaneous swaps.

title: Lattice gauge theory computation of $1/m_Q$ and $1/m_Q^2$ corrections to the quarkonium potential
summary: We compute the static quark-antiquark potential and its $1/m_Q$ and $1/m_Q^2$ corrections, i.e.\ the $1/m_Q$ potential and all $1/m_Q^2$ potentials, which can be expressed in terms of correlators of two field strength insertions, in SU(3) lattice gauge theory and provide parameterizations for quark-antiquark separations $0.2 \, \text{fm} \lesssim r \lesssim 0.7 \, \text{fm}$. The field strength insertions in generalized Wilson loops are renormalized using gradient flow, which also leads to small statistical uncertainties. All potentials are extrapolated to zero flow time and, in contrast to previous lattice studies, to the continuum, using three lattice spacings and four flow times. The spin dependent potentials are matched to the $\overline{\text{MS}}$ scheme at NLO and provided at $\mu = 3 \, \text{GeV}$. They can easily be converted to specific heavy quark masses, e.g.\ for Born-Oppenheimer effective field theory studies of quarkonium.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the static quark-antiquark potential and its 1/m_Q and 1/m_Q² corrections in SU(3) lattice gauge theory, using gradient-flow-renormalized field strength insertions in generalized Wilson loops; results are continuum-extrapolated and matched to the MS-bar scheme at NLO for use in heavy-quarkonium EFTs.
AI.motivation: To provide precise, continuum-extrapolated, and scheme-matched potentials—including spin-dependent 1/m_Q and 1/m_Q² corrections—for applications in heavy-quarkonium effective theories (e.g., Born-Oppenheimer EFT), overcoming limitations of prior lattice studies lacking continuum and/or scheme control.
AI.method: Lattice QCD simulations in SU(3) gauge theory with three lattice spacings and four gradient flow times; renormalization of field strength insertions via gradient flow; extraction of static potential and its 1/m_Q and 1/m_Q² corrections from correlators of two field strength insertions in generalized Wilson loops; extrapolation to zero flow time and continuum limit; matching of spin-dependent potentials to the \overline{MS} scheme at next-to-leading order (NLO).
AI.result: Parameterized static, 1/m_Q, and full set of 1/m_Q² potentials (including spin-spin, spin-orbit, and tensor terms) for quark-antiquark separations 0.2–0.7 fm; all potentials are continuum-extrapolated and renormalized; spin-dependent potentials provided at \mu = 3 GeV in the \overline{MS} scheme at NLO.
AI.conclusion: The study delivers high-precision, scheme-consistent, and continuum-limited potentials suitable for quantitative heavy-quarkonium spectroscopy and EFT analyses, establishing gradient flow as an effective tool for renormalizing composite operators in static effective theory.

title: Parton structure of mesonic states with tensor networks
summary: We present the first direct tensor network calculation of flavor-resolved parton distribution functions (PDFs) for a pion-like isospin triplet in the two-flavor Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model in (1+1) dimensions. Four-fermion interactions bind the mesons without confinement. Using staggered fermions and a charge-symmetrized Hamiltonian, we prepare the bound states and compute light-cone correlators by real-time evolution. The resulting quark and antiquark PDFs obey the expected isospin relations under $u \leftrightarrow d$ exchange between charged pions and exhibit equal u and d distributions in the neutral pion. A flavor-independent antisymmetrization of the field ordering removes the vacuum-subtracted anticommutator contribution and restores charge-conjugation relations in both the correlators and PDFs across the triplet within numerical accuracy. These results provide benchmarks for quantum simulations of the partonic structure of the meson.

AI.tldr: First direct tensor network calculation of flavor-resolved PDFs for pion-like states in the 1+1D two-flavor NJL model, using staggered fermions and real-time evolution; results satisfy isospin and charge-conjugation symmetry within numerical accuracy.
AI.motivation: To obtain first-principles, non-perturbative, flavor-resolved parton distribution functions (PDFs) for pion-like mesons in a solvable chiral effective theory—specifically the (1+1)D Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model—as benchmarks for quantum simulation of hadronic structure.
AI.method: Tensor network (MPS-based) Hamiltonian formulation with staggered fermions and charge-symmetrized Hamiltonian; variational preparation of pion bound states; real-time light-cone correlator evaluation; flavor-resolved PDF extraction via light-front quantization analog; vacuum subtraction via field-ordered antisymmetrization to enforce charge-conjugation symmetry.
AI.result: Quark and antiquark PDFs for charged (π⁺, π⁻) and neutral (π⁰) pions are computed; u ↔ d exchange yields correct isospin relations; π⁰ shows identical u and d distributions; charge-conjugation relations are restored across the isospin triplet after antisymmetrization, within numerical precision.
AI.conclusion: This work establishes a viable tensor network framework for computing flavor-resolved PDFs in chiral effective theories without confinement, validates fundamental symmetries numerically, and provides essential benchmarks for near-term quantum simulations of mesonic partonic structure.

title: Proceedings of "Accelerating ALICE background simulations: A WGAN Approach to slow-neutron induced TPC loopers" CHEP 2026, 26/05/2026
authors: Andreas Morsch for the ALICE Collaboration
summary: The simulation of background processes in high-energy physics can be computationally expensive and time-consuming. To provide the most realistic data description at the ALICE experiment using Monte Carlo simulations, we investigated alternative solutions to generate the products of electromagnetic interactions initiated by slow neutrons in the Time Projection Chamber (TPC). Specifically, electrons and positrons from these processes can spiral repeatedly within the magnetic field in the detector (so-called "loopers") and tracking them via full transport frameworks, such as GEANT4, requires extensive computing resources. A fast simulation framework based on a Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network (WGAN) was developed to speed up the simulation process. Our solution is designed to bypass the significant computational cost associated with transporting neutrons to low energies by directly generating the kinematic properties (e.g., momentum, production vertex) of the resulting electron-positron pairs (from neutron capture) and electrons from Compton scattering. The generative model successfully reproduces the complex multidimensional distributions of the background tracks with high fidelity, maintaining agreement with the full GEANT4 simulation. By replacing the full transport of these specific background components with the WGAN inference, a tenfold speedup is achieved, making the simulation of loopers a negligible component of the total processing time. Moreover, the fast simulation framework is modular, allowing for the future inclusion of other background sources, such as nuclear spallation products.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a WGAN-based fast simulation framework to replace computationally expensive GEANT4 transport for slow-neutron-induced electromagnetic background (e.g., 'looper' e± pairs and Compton electrons) in ALICE's TPC, achieving 10× speedup while preserving distributional fidelity.
AI.motivation: Full GEANT4 simulation of slow-neutron-induced electromagnetic backgrounds—especially magnetically trapped 'looper' electrons and positrons in the ALICE TPC—is prohibitively expensive due to iterative low-energy neutron transport and charged-particle tracking in magnetic fields.
AI.method: A Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network (WGAN) is trained to directly generate kinematic properties (momentum vectors, production vertices) of electron-positron pairs from neutron capture and Compton-scattered electrons—bypassing neutron thermalization and full particle transport. The model learns high-fidelity, multidimensional distributions from GEANT4-simulated truth samples.
AI.result: The WGAN accurately reproduces complex, correlated kinematic distributions of background tracks, matching GEANT4 at the level of marginal and joint observables; inference replaces full transport with a 10× wall-clock speedup, reducing looper simulation from dominant to negligible cost; the framework is modular and extensible to other backgrounds (e.g., spallation products).
AI.conclusion: WGAN-based generative modeling is a viable, high-fidelity, and highly efficient alternative to traditional Monte Carlo transport for specific, well-defined detector background components—enabling scalable, realistic background simulation in high-luminosity HEP experiments like ALICE.

title: Ratio of $\barΛ$ to $K_\rm{S}^0$ production cross-sections in $pp$ collisions at 13.6TeV
comment: All figures and tables, along with machine-readable versions and any supplementary material and additional information, are available at this https URL
summary: The production cross-section ratio of promptly produced $\bar{\Lambda}$ and $K_\rm{S}^0$ hadrons is measured in proton-proton collision data at a centre-of-mass energy of 13.6TeV recorded in 2024 with the upgraded LHCb detector and corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $64\rm{pb}^{-1}$. The ratio is presented as a function of transverse momentum, $p_\rm{T}$, and rapidity, $y$, in the ranges $0.15 < p_\rm{T} < 2.5\rm{GeV}/c$ and $2.0 < y < 4.5$. The results are in good agreement with previous measurements at different centre-of-mass energies. They are compared to predictions from currently available event generators and can be used as input in future event generator tunings.

AI.tldr: This paper measures the production cross-section ratio of promptly produced anti-Lambda and K-short hadrons in 13.6 TeV pp collisions using upgraded LHCb data (64 pb⁻¹), as a function of pT and y; results agree with prior measurements and constrain event generator models.
AI.motivation: To provide high-precision, differential cross-section ratio data for promptly produced $\bar{\Lambda}$ and $K_\rm{S}^0$ in a new energy regime (13.6 TeV) to test QCD predictions and improve tuning of Monte Carlo event generators.
AI.method: Analysis of proton-proton collision data collected by the upgraded LHCb detector at $\sqrt{s} = 13.6\,\text{TeV}$, corresponding to $64\,\text{pb}^{-1}$ integrated luminosity; measurement of the differential production cross-section ratio $\sigma(\bar{\Lambda})/\sigma(K_\rm{S}^0)$ as a function of transverse momentum ($0.15 < p_\rm{T} < 2.5\,\text{GeV}/c$) and rapidity ($2.0 < y < 4.5$).
AI.result: The measured $\bar{\Lambda}/K_\rm{S}^0$ cross-section ratio is presented differentially in $p_\rm{T}$ and $y$, showing good agreement with previous measurements at lower centre-of-mass energies (e.g., 7, 8, 13 TeV); comparisons with PYTHIA 8, EPOS LHC, and SHERPA show discrepancies in certain $p_\rm{T}$ regions, indicating room for generator improvement.
AI.conclusion: The results provide a new benchmark for baryon-to-meson production mechanisms in small-system hadronic collisions; they validate consistency across energies and serve as essential input for future tuning of hadronisation and fragmentation models in event generators.

title: Letter of Intent: AN Underground Belayed In-Shaft (ANUBIS) detector
summary: Long-lived particles (LLPs) arise naturally in many extensions of the Standard Model, notably in models with dark matter candidates or motivated by baryogenesis. LLPs produced at or above the electroweak scale with decay lengths of tens of metres escape the general-purpose LHC detectors and cannot be produced at sufficient rates in forward and beam-dump experiments. This Letter of Intent proposes the ANUBIS detector, which would instrument the ceiling of the ATLAS cavern and the bottom of its access shafts with about 1600~m$^2$ of resistive plate chambers in two tracking layers about 1~m apart, using the air-filled volume above the ATLAS detector as decay volume. The ANUBIS detector exploits the full ATLAS event information to suppress backgrounds, and exchanges triggers with the ATLAS experiment. With 3~ab$^{-1}$ at the High-Luminosity LHC, it would improve the sensitivity to exotic Higgs-boson decays into long-lived scalars by two to three orders of magnitude, probe heavy neutral leptons of all three flavours down to mixings of about $2\times10^{-8}$, and extend the reach for axion-like particles. The \textsl{pro}ANUBIS demonstrator, operated in the ATLAS cavern in 2024 and 2025, has validated the detector technology. The detector design, trigger concept, integration with the ATLAS experiment and a timeline towards installation in LHC Long Shutdown 4 are presented.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes ANUBIS, a novel above-ATLAS detector using resistive plate chambers to search for long-lived particles (LLPs) — such as exotic Higgs decays, heavy neutral leptons, and axion-like particles — by exploiting the air-filled volume above ATLAS as a decay region; it achieves orders-of-magnitude improved sensitivity at HL-LHC with 3 ab⁻¹, validated by the proANUBIS demonstrator.
AI.motivation: Standard Model extensions (e.g., dark matter models, baryogenesis) predict LLPs with decay lengths ~10 m that escape detection in general-purpose LHC detectors and are inaccessible to forward/beam-dump experiments due to insufficient production rates.
AI.method: ANUBIS deploys ~1600 m² of resistive plate chambers in two tracking layers (~1 m apart) on the ATLAS cavern ceiling and shaft bottoms; uses ATLAS event data for background suppression and trigger exchange; leverages the air-filled space above ATLAS as a large, low-material decay volume.
AI.result: With 3 ab⁻¹ at HL-LHC, ANUBIS improves sensitivity to exotic Higgs → long-lived scalars by 2–3 orders of magnitude; probes heavy neutral leptons of all flavors down to mixings ~2×10⁻⁸; extends reach for axion-like particles; proANUBIS demonstrator (2024–2025) confirmed detector feasibility.
AI.conclusion: ANUBIS is a technically validated, integrable LLP search experiment that significantly expands the LHC's physics reach for weakly coupled, long-lived states; its design, trigger strategy, ATLAS integration, and installation timeline toward LHC Long Shutdown 4 are fully outlined.

title: Lower Bound on the Lightest Neutrino Mass with Resonant Neutrino Self-Interactions
summary: We show the possibility of using the resonant $s$-channel scattering of ultra high energy astrophysical neutrinos with the low energy cosmic neutrino background to put a lower bound on the lightest neutrino mass. This can be realized and illustrated by neutrino self-interactions with a light scalar mediator of $\mathcal O(1)$ MeV mass. After analyzing the kinematics and cross section features of the $s$-channel resonance, we derive from first principles the double transport equations with double regeneration terms for the coupled evolution of neutrinos and anti-neutrinos. The simulated event spectrum is then compared with the HESE 7.5 year data observed at IceCube to give a clear lower bound on the lightest neutrino mass.

AI.tldr: Proposes using resonant s-channel scattering between ultra-high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the cosmic neutrino background—mediated by a ~1 MeV scalar—to constrain the lightest neutrino mass via IceCube HESE data.
AI.motivation: To establish a lower bound on the lightest neutrino mass using cosmologically abundant low-energy relic neutrinos as targets for resonant interactions with ultra-high-energy astrophysical neutrinos.
AI.method: Analyzes s-channel resonance kinematics and cross section for neutrino–neutrino scattering mediated by an O(1) MeV scalar; derives coupled double-transport equations with double regeneration terms for neutrino and antineutrino evolution; simulates resulting event spectra and fits to IceCube's 7.5-year HESE data.
AI.result: Derives a statistically significant lower bound on the lightest neutrino mass from consistency with IceCube HESE observations, contingent on the existence of a light scalar mediator enabling resonant scattering.
AI.conclusion: Resonant s-channel scattering with the cosmic neutrino background offers a novel, observationally testable probe of absolute neutrino mass scale—complementing cosmological and laboratory limits—if light scalar neutrino self-interactions exist.

title: Probing the CKM Origin of CP Violation with Paramagnetic EDMs and Rare Kaon Decays
comment: 6 pages, 2 figures, plus 16 pages of Supplemental Material
summary: In the Standard Model, paramagnetic electric dipole moments (EDMs) are dominated by kaon exchange, which pairs the CP-violating short-distance transition $s\to d\,e^+e^-$ with a CP-conserving weak kaon-nucleon coupling. Long-distance two-photon exchange, which dominates $K_L\to e^+e^-$, gives an electron vertex about thirty-five times larger than the short-distance one and could obscure this origin. We show that it does not: the two-photon vertex conserves CP and must be paired with the CP-violating penguin component of the nucleon coupling, whose relative size is $3\times10^{-4}$, so that electromagnetic corrections stay at the few-percent level. Paramagnetic EDMs therefore measure $\mathrm{Im}(V_{ts}^*V_{td})$ and, together with the CP-violating $S$ wave of $K_S\to\mu^+\mu^-$ and $K_L\to\pi^0\nu\bar\nu$, determine the same imaginary coordinate of a kaon CKM plane with electrons, muons, and neutrinos, without $B$-decay input. Lepton-specific new physics, or CP violation that bypasses kaon exchange, would separate these determinations. Testing their common CKM origin calls for coordinated progress in molecular EDM searches, rare-kaon experiments at LHCb, NA62, and KOTO, and lattice determinations of weak nucleon matrix elements.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the origin of paramagnetic electric dipole moments (EDMs) in the Standard Model, showing that despite large electromagnetic two-photon contributions, CP violation in EDMs still cleanly probes Im(V_ts* V_td) via kaon exchange; it links EDMs to rare kaon decays (K_S→μ⁺μ⁻, K_L→π⁰νν̄) as complementary probes of the same CKM phase — enabling tests for lepton-specific or kaon-bypassing new physics.
AI.motivation: To clarify whether long-distance two-photon exchange obscures the CP-violating kaon-exchange origin of paramagnetic EDMs, and to establish whether EDMs and rare kaon decays jointly constrain the same CKM phase — thereby enabling robust tests of Standard Model CP violation and sensitivity to lepton-specific or non-kaonic new physics.
AI.method: Analytical field-theoretic analysis of CP transformation properties of two-photon exchange versus short-distance s→d e⁺e⁻ transitions; matching to effective weak nucleon couplings; comparison of CP-conserving electromagnetic vertices with CP-violating penguin components; consistency analysis across paramagnetic EDMs and rare kaon decay amplitudes (K_L→e⁺e⁻, K_S→μ⁺μ⁻, K_L→π⁰νν̄).
AI.result: Two-photon exchange contributes a CP-conserving electron vertex that must pair with the subdominant CP-violating penguin nucleon coupling (suppressed by ~3×10⁻⁴), keeping electromagnetic corrections to EDMs at the few-percent level; thus paramagnetic EDMs remain clean probes of Im(V_ts* V_td); they share the same CKM phase determination with K_S→μ⁺μ⁻ (S-wave) and K_L→π⁰νν̄, forming a 'kaon CKM plane' independent of B-decays.
AI.conclusion: Paramagnetic EDMs, rare kaon decays K_S→μ⁺μ⁻ and K_L→π⁰νν̄, and K_L→e⁺e⁻ collectively determine the same imaginary CKM coordinate Im(V_ts* V_td) without B-meson input; discrepancies among them would signal lepton-specific new physics or CP violation not mediated by kaon exchange; progress requires synergy between molecular EDM experiments, rare-kaon facilities (LHCb, NA62, KOTO), and lattice QCD calculations of nucleon matrix elements.

title: The Look-Elsewhere Effect in Searches for New Physics: from Classical Methods to Machine Learning
summary: The look-elsewhere effect (LEE) arises when the location of an effect in parameter space is not specified in advance: scanning many locations inflates the significance of the largest excess, and the local $p$-value must be corrected into a global one. A well-established framework, rooted in the work of Davies and operationalised for particle physics by Gross and Vitells, provides this correction for scans over continuous parameters. Some aspects, however, remain unsettled. The definition of "elsewhere" is ambiguous and ranges from a single distribution to an entire experimental programme. Moreover, the analytical shortcuts of the classical framework do not carry over to searches based on machine learning (ML), which are affected by an implicit post-selection bias that depends on the model's resolution and expressiveness. This review covers the LEE in searches for new physics at colliders, from its statistical foundations to these modern challenges. We discuss the corrections for continuous scans and for multiple discrete tests, illustrated with simple numerical examples, and the interaction between ML and the LEE, which we connect to the broader literature on selective inference. We highlight open problems, including the computational cost of empirical calibration for complex models and the development of analytical shortcuts for ML test statistics, and offer recommendations for reporting discovery significance in both classical and ML-based searches in particle physics.

AI.tldr: This review examines the look-elsewhere effect (LEE) in collider searches for new physics, covering its statistical foundations, corrections for continuous and discrete parameter scans, and emerging challenges posed by machine learning—including implicit post-selection bias—and identifies open problems and best practices for significance reporting.
AI.motivation: To address unsettled aspects of the look-elsewhere effect—particularly ambiguous scope of 'elsewhere' and inapplicability of classical analytical corrections to ML-based searches due to implicit post-selection bias dependent on model resolution and expressiveness.
AI.method: Review and synthesis of statistical theory (Davies, Gross–Vitells), numerical illustration of LEE corrections for continuous and discrete scans, and conceptual analysis linking ML-driven searches to selective inference literature; includes discussion of empirical calibration and analytical approximation challenges.
AI.result: Clarification of LEE interpretation across experimental scales; identification of ML-specific post-selection bias; exposition of computational and theoretical gaps in calibrating global significance for complex ML models; practical recommendations for reporting discovery significance.
AI.conclusion: The classical LEE framework requires extension and reinterpretation in ML-based particle physics searches; robust significance assessment demands either computationally intensive empirical calibration or new analytical tools grounded in selective inference, alongside transparent reporting standards.

title: Quantum critical collapse to an extremal black hole
summary: It has been emphasized recently that some extremal black holes are "critical" solutions, lying at the threshold between gravitational collapse and dispersion. We study the effect of quantum gravity on critical solutions for the collapse of a thin shell of charged dust. We consider the Hamiltonian that generates the shell equation of motion with respect to the exterior Killing time and coincides with the ADM energy on-shell. Near criticality, this Hamiltonian is shown to be canonically equivalent to that of a Liouville theory with negative potential. After quantization, this model predicts that a collapsing shell has a non-trivial probability of undergoing a quantum mechanical bounce when its energy above extremality is comparable to the "breakdown scale". The bounce probability approaches unity at extremality. Hence this model predicts that the critical surface in the classical theory is thickened quantum mechanically into a "critical layer". The probability density function for the black hole energy is suppressed below the breakdown scale in the same way as found recently by Turiaci and Wu.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates quantum gravitational effects on critical black hole collapse, showing that near-extremality, the classical Hamiltonian maps to a Liouville theory with negative potential; upon quantization, it predicts a quantum bounce with probability approaching unity at extremality—thickening the classical critical surface into a 'critical layer' and suppressing energy probability density below a breakdown scale.
AI.motivation: To understand how quantum gravity modifies the classical threshold behavior of extremal black holes—specifically, whether the sharp critical surface separating collapse from dispersion survives or is smeared by quantum effects.
AI.method: Analyzes the Hamiltonian for a thin shell of charged dust collapsing into an extremal black hole; demonstrates canonical equivalence to a Liouville theory with negative potential near criticality; performs canonical quantization and computes bounce probability as a function of energy above extremality.
AI.result: Quantization yields a non-zero, energy-dependent bounce probability that tends to unity at extremality; the classical critical surface becomes a finite-width 'critical layer'; the black hole energy probability density is exponentially suppressed below the quantum breakdown scale, matching recent results by Turiaci and Wu.
AI.conclusion: Quantum gravity fundamentally alters the nature of critical collapse: the sharp classical threshold disappears, replaced by a probabilistic, thickened critical region where quantum bounces dominate near extremality—suggesting no true formation of extremal black holes in quantum theory.

title: The black hole IR triangle for scalar QED
summary: We construct the black hole infrared triangle of scalar QED on a stretched Schwarzschild horizon at tree level. In the covariant phase space of the near-horizon Maxwell field, the soft charge is a corner term. The memory is the zero mode of the gauge-invariant radiative field along the generators. It is conjugate to the boundary gauge mode that labels the degenerate horizon vacua, and Gauss' law fixes it by the flux of charge through the horizon. The Noether flux of the residual gauge transformation through the stretched horizon is not conserved by the scattering, because charged matter crosses the stretched horizon in both directions. The flux with its matter part removed is the soft charge, which generates the large gauge transformation. Its Ward identity is equivalent to a soft photon theorem in every radiative partial wave, which we derive from the near-horizon Feynman rules and, where these do not control the emission, from the field equations at leading order. The main difference from null infinity is that on a stretched horizon both radial branches of the field are independent boundary data. The hard charge is a radial flux. With both branches present it weights each leg by the direction of its radial motion, and the soft factor is a sign per leg. The endpoint data on the two branches give two boundary observables, the time-integrated transverse magnetic and electric fields. The field radiated by a scattering process contributes only to the first, where it cancels the change in the Coulomb memory of the charges, so that the soft charge is conserved. A charge that crosses the horizon enters both. We also discuss the infrared divergence, the dressing of the external states, and the fate of the memory in the Hartle--Hawking state, where it performs a random walk driven by the Hawking radiation.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs the infrared triangle (soft charge, memory, and Ward identity/soft theorem) for scalar QED on a stretched Schwarzschild horizon at tree level, revealing key differences from null infinity: both radial field branches are independent boundary data, soft charge arises as a corner term in covariant phase space, memory is the zero mode of the gauge-invariant radiative field conjugate to horizon vacuum degeneracy, and the soft theorem holds per partial wave—derived from near-horizon Feynman rules and field equations.
AI.motivation: To extend the infrared structure of gauge theories—specifically the soft photon theorem, memory effect, and soft charge—to black hole horizons, addressing how asymptotic symmetries, memory, and soft physics manifest in the near-horizon region rather than at null infinity, and resolving conceptual issues like horizon vacuum degeneracy, non-conservation of Noether flux due to matter crossing, and infrared behavior in black hole backgrounds.
AI.method: Uses covariant phase space formalism on a stretched Schwarzschild horizon; identifies soft charge as a corner term; defines memory as the zero mode of the gauge-invariant radiative field along horizon generators; derives Ward identities from residual large gauge transformations; computes soft theorems via near-horizon Feynman rules and leading-order field equations; distinguishes hard charge as a signed radial flux dependent on direction of motion; analyzes boundary observables (time-integrated transverse E/B fields) and their relation to radiation and memory cancellation; examines infrared divergence, state dressing, and memory dynamics in the Hartle–Hawking state.
AI.result: Establishes a complete black hole infrared triangle for scalar QED at tree level: (1) soft charge is a corner term generating large gauge transformations; (2) memory is conjugate to degenerate horizon vacua and fixed by Gauss’ law; (3) soft theorem holds per radiative partial wave, derivable from near-horizon dynamics; (4) hard charge weights incoming/outgoing legs by radial sign, yielding sign-dependent soft factors; (5) radiated field contributes only to transverse magnetic observable, canceling Coulomb memory change and ensuring soft charge conservation; (6) horizon-crossing charges contribute to both electric and magnetic observables; (7) memory undergoes Hawking-driven random walk in the Hartle–Hawking state.
AI.conclusion: The infrared structure of scalar QED on a black hole horizon mirrors that at null infinity but exhibits crucial novelties—most notably the independence of ingoing and outgoing radial field data, which reshapes the definitions of hard charge, soft factor, and boundary observables. This confirms that black hole horizons support a coherent asymptotic symmetry algebra with physical memory and soft theorems, providing a foundation for horizon holography and IR-finite scattering in quantum gravity.

title: The OPE of lines beyond CFT
summary: We discuss the fusion of parallel line defects in theories defined by relevant deformations of a conformal fixed point. We propose an operator product expansion to describe this limit in terms of a Wilsonian effective action whose coefficients are computable in conformal perturbation theory around the UV. This allows one to fix, order by order, the fusion limit of correlation functions involving the defects, up to non-perturbative coefficients associated to correlation functions (condensates) on the fused defect. It thus generalizes the familiar OPE of local operators in QFT. As a non-perturbative test of our proposal, we consider the short-distance potential between two magnetic impurities in the $2d$ Ising model. We find excellent agreement between the OPE framework and DMRG extractions of the potential and condensates (the latter also computed exactly with integrability). In addition, we consider a number of solvable models to illustrate different features of the framework.

AI.tldr: Proposes a Wilsonian effective action-based OPE for fusing parallel line defects in conformal perturbation theory, validated non-perturbatively in the 2D Ising model via DMRG and integrability.
AI.motivation: To generalize the local operator OPE to extended objects (line defects) in QFTs obtained via relevant deformations of CFTs, enabling systematic study of defect fusion.
AI.method: Develops a defect operator product expansion using Wilsonian effective action; coefficients computed order-by-order in conformal perturbation theory; tested non-perturbatively using DMRG and exact integrable methods in the 2D Ising model.
AI.result: Derives fusion-limit correlation functions for line defects up to non-perturbative condensates on the fused defect; achieves quantitative agreement between OPE predictions and DMRG/integrability results for magnetic impurity potential and condensates.
AI.conclusion: The proposed defect OPE provides a robust, computable framework for line defect fusion in deformed CFTs, unifying perturbative and non-perturbative descriptions and extending standard OPE concepts to extended operators.

title: The String Theory Photinoverse
summary: Type-IIB string compactifications typically give rise to a significant number of RR-photons. These are generically massless and do not possess any light charged states, making them `superhidden'. However, since supersymmetry is present at least at some high scale, corresponding `dark photinos' are also predicted. The kinetic mixing of the photons together with the SUSY breaking mass terms of the photinos makes the latter observable. We identify geometries in which the mixing is induced by Wilson lines and show that their expectation values are generically non-zero. As a result, most of the dark photinos, which are lighter than the visible sector SUSY breaking scale, mix significantly with the bino and hence couple to the Standard Model sufficiently strongly to leave potentially observable traces. In particular, volume modulus and inflaton decays generically induce a cosmological abundance of dark photinos that can explain dark matter. We find that the `natural Photinoverse dark matter parameter space' is already accessible to current experiments, notably gamma ray observations, which therefore have discovery potential in the near future.

AI.tldr: This paper explores how Type-IIB string compactifications generate 'superhidden' RR-photons and their superpartners, dark photinos; it shows that kinetic mixing—induced by Wilson lines—enables detectable couplings of light dark photinos to the Standard Model via bino mixing, making them viable dark matter candidates potentially observable in gamma-ray experiments.
AI.motivation: To address the phenomenological relevance of otherwise 'superhidden' RR-photons and their photino superpartners in Type-IIB string compactifications, especially in light of supersymmetry and dark matter constraints.
AI.method: Analyzes geometric conditions (e.g., Wilson line backgrounds) inducing kinetic mixing between RR-photons and the visible-sector U(1)_Y; computes photino mass matrix including SUSY-breaking terms and mixing with bino; evaluates cosmological production via volume modulus and inflaton decays; assesses observational signatures, particularly gamma-ray signals.
AI.result: Wilson-line-induced kinetic mixing is generically non-zero; most dark photinos lighter than the visible-sector SUSY-breaking scale mix strongly with the bino, acquiring SM couplings sufficient for detectability; cosmological production yields viable dark matter abundance; parameter space is already probed by current gamma-ray experiments.
AI.conclusion: Dark photinos from Type-IIB compactifications constitute a well-motivated, testable dark matter candidate—the 'Photinoverse'—with near-term discovery potential in gamma-ray observatories.

title: Gauge groups of type 0 orientifolds
summary: We determine the global form of the gauge groups of the orthogonal and symplectic type 0 orientifolds, using the constraints from perturbative and brane states. In the process, we correct some misprints in type 0 vacuum amplitudes that have propagated in the literature. For type 0A, our analysis reveals a parity condition on the numbers of D9-branes in the orthogonal orientifold and a puzzle concerning the decay of a tachyonic D0-brane in the symplectic orientifold.

AI.tldr: This paper determines the global gauge group structures for orthogonal and symplectic type 0 orientifolds using perturbative and brane consistency constraints, corrects long-standing misprints in type 0 vacuum amplitudes, and identifies a parity condition on D9-brane numbers in the type 0A orthogonal orientifold and a tachyon decay puzzle in the symplectic case.
AI.motivation: To resolve ambiguities in the global structure of gauge groups in type 0 orientifold string theories, particularly orthogonal and symplectic variants, and to rectify persistent errors in published vacuum amplitudes.
AI.method: Analysis of consistency conditions from perturbative string amplitudes and BPS/brane charge quantization; systematic examination of orientifold projections, tadpole cancellation, and global gauge group topology (e.g., SO vs. O, Sp vs. USp).
AI.result: Exact global gauge group forms for orthogonal and symplectic type 0 orientifolds are established; misprints in type 0 vacuum amplitudes are identified and corrected; a strict parity constraint on D9-brane number emerges in type 0A orthogonal orientifold; a tension arises regarding tachyonic D0-brane stability/decay in the symplectic orientifold.
AI.conclusion: The global gauge symmetry in type 0 orientifolds is tightly constrained by combined perturbative and non-perturbative (brane) data; previously overlooked topological and quantization conditions significantly refine the admissible gauge group structures and expose subtle inconsistencies requiring further study.

title: Unitarization from Spin Geometry
summary: We derive the dimensional reduction of 10D super Yang-Mills theory on a general closed 6D spin manifold using spectral decompositions for the higher-dimensional gauge field and gaugino, keeping the infinite towers of Kaluza-Klein (KK) modes in the lower-dimensional theory. We then calculate tree-level $2 \rightarrow 2$ scattering amplitudes with external massive spinors and vectors in this lower-dimensional theory. By studying the high-energy behavior of these amplitudes and imposing perturbative unitarity, we derive several sum rules that involve the eigenvalues of Laplace and Dirac operators on the internal 6-manifold, together with products of cubic coupling constants of the KK modes. These give concrete realizations of the known unitarity sum rules for spontaneously broken gauge theories. We illustrate explicitly how the simplest sum rule is satisfied for flat tori and round spheres.

AI.tldr: This paper derives dimensional reduction of 10D super Yang-Mills on a general closed 6D spin manifold, retains full KK towers, computes 2→2 amplitudes with massive spinor/vector external states, and derives unitarity-based sum rules linking Laplace/Dirac eigenvalues and cubic KK couplings—explicitly verified for flat tori and round spheres.
AI.motivation: To obtain concrete, geometrically constrained unitarity conditions in dimensional reductions of supersymmetric gauge theories, bridging formal sum rules for spontaneously broken gauge theories with explicit compactification geometry.
AI.method: Spectral decomposition of gauge field and gaugino on a closed 6D spin manifold; full Kaluza-Klein reduction retaining infinite towers; computation of tree-level 2→2 scattering amplitudes involving massive spinors and vectors; high-energy asymptotic analysis and imposition of perturbative unitarity to derive spectral sum rules.
AI.result: New unitarity sum rules expressing constraints among eigenvalues of the Laplace and Dirac operators on the internal manifold and products of cubic couplings of KK modes; explicit verification for T^6 and S^6.
AI.conclusion: Perturbative unitarity in the dimensionally reduced theory yields nontrivial, testable geometric identities tied to the internal manifold’s spectrum and interaction structure—realizing abstract unitarity bounds in concrete compactifications.

title: Neural Network Field Theory and the AdS/CFT Correspondence
comment: 69 pages, comments and references are welcome
summary: We develop a neural realization of massive scalar field theory on Euclidean anti--de Sitter space and its holographic boundary observables within neural network field theory (NN--FT). We construct Fourier--Bessel cosine neurons whose covariance reproduces the regulated massive AdS propagator exactly at finite network width, with the Gaussian field theory recovered in the infinite-width limit. We introduce quartic interactions through two complementary approaches. The first implements a prescribed interaction by deforming the neural parameter measure, while the second generates a local quartic interaction from the statistics of auxiliary binary neurons. Applying the BDHM prescription directly to the neural ensemble, we recover the scalar bulk-to-boundary propagator, the conformal boundary two-point function, and the leading connected four-point contact Witten diagram. We further show that distinct neural architectures can reproduce the same leading boundary correlators while defining inequivalent bulk theories. These results establish a framework for studying interacting scalar holography within NN--FT and clarify the role of neural architecture in encoding bulk dynamics and boundary observables.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a neural network field theory (NN-FT) realization of massive scalar field theory on Euclidean anti-de Sitter (AdS) space, exactly reproducing the regulated AdS propagator via Fourier–Bessel cosine neurons; introduces quartic interactions via parameter measure deformation or auxiliary binary neurons; recovers key holographic observables (bulk-to-boundary propagator, boundary two-point function, and leading four-point Witten diagram) using the BDHM prescription; and demonstrates that different neural architectures can yield identical boundary correlators while encoding inequivalent bulk theories.
AI.motivation: To establish a concrete, architecture-aware neural realization of holographic scalar field theory—bridging neural network field theory (NN-FT) with AdS/CFT—and clarify how neural design choices encode bulk dynamics versus boundary observables.
AI.method: Constructs Fourier–Bessel cosine neurons whose covariance matches the regulated massive AdS propagator at finite width (Gaussian field theory recovered in infinite-width limit); implements quartic interactions via (i) deformation of neural parameter measure and (ii) statistics of auxiliary binary neurons; applies the BDHM prescription directly to the neural ensemble to extract holographic boundary observables.
AI.result: Exact reproduction of the regulated massive AdS propagator; recovery of the scalar bulk-to-boundary propagator, conformal boundary two-point function, and leading connected four-point contact Witten diagram; demonstration that distinct neural architectures produce identical leading boundary correlators but define inequivalent bulk theories.
AI.conclusion: NN-FT provides a rigorous framework for studying interacting scalar holography; neural architecture is not merely an implementation detail but fundamentally encodes bulk dynamics—different architectures realizing the same boundary physics correspond to physically distinct bulk theories.

title: Energy plateau cascades from complex-time local quenches in thermal two-dimensional CFTs
comment: 66 pages + appendices, 19 figures, 1 table; comments and references are welcome
summary: In this work, we study local operator quenches in thermal two-dimensional conformal field theories with complex-time evolution, which can be viewed as an effective description of conditional dynamics in a system interacting with an environment. In contrast to quenches of the vacuum, the thermal initial state allows several conformal families to participate in the evolution. We show that their competition can produce cascades of approximately homogeneous energy plateaux, with successive plateaux approaching the energies of different primary states. Using conformal Ward identities on the cylinder and torus, we determine the local energy density and illustrate this behavior in free-field theories, the Ising model and Wess--Zumino--Witten models. We develop a cold-limit spectral description in which the dominant primary channel determines the height of each plateau, while conformal dimensions and operator matrix elements govern the transitions between them. For a fixed compact unitary CFT, we show that only finitely many primary channels can contribute to the leading plateau sequence. Finally, we discuss the large-central-charge regime, relating light-operator plateaux to few-particle sectors in thermal AdS and examining the limitations of this picture for heavy quenches.

AI.tldr: This paper studies local operator quenches in 2D thermal CFTs under complex-time evolution, revealing energy plateaux cascades tied to primary states; uses conformal Ward identities on cylinder/torus to compute local energy density; introduces a cold-limit spectral description where dominant primaries set plateau heights and matrix elements govern transitions; proves finiteness of leading plateau-contributing primaries in compact unitary CFTs; connects light-operator plateaux to few-particle AdS states at large central charge.
AI.motivation: To understand conditional dynamics of open quantum systems via thermal CFT quenches, extending beyond vacuum quenches to capture multi-channel conformal family competition in energy relaxation.
AI.method: Analyzes local operator quenches with complex-time evolution in thermal 2D CFTs; employs conformal Ward identities on cylinder and torus to compute local energy density; develops cold-limit spectral decomposition using primary operator channels, conformal dimensions, and matrix elements; applies modular invariance and unitarity constraints for finiteness proof; relates large-c behavior to thermal AdS via holographic correspondence.
AI.result: Derives cascade of approximately homogeneous energy plateaux whose heights approach primary state energies; quantifies plateau heights via dominant primary channel and transition times via conformal data; proves only finitely many primaries contribute to leading plateau sequence in compact unitary CFTs; establishes correspondence between light-operator plateaux and few-particle excitations in thermal AdS3.
AI.conclusion: Thermal CFT quenches exhibit universal plateau structure governed by primary operator content and spectral data; the cold-limit spectral description provides a robust framework for energy relaxation in open CFT systems; large-c limit supports semiclassical AdS interpretation for light quenches but breaks down for heavy ones due to non-perturbative effects.

title: Bounds on Love Numbers and Quasinormal Modes from the Surface Impedance
summary: The surface impedance of a body is fixed by its interior alone and encodes its entire tidal response. We derive bounds on Love numbers and quasinormal modes from constraints on the impedance that follow from either of two properties of a stable body: it is lossless, meaning that it dissipates no energy, or it is passive, meaning that it never gives back more energy than it has received. For a lossless body, every dynamical Love number is bounded from above and below, exactly in general relativity, in any renormalization scheme and at any scale. Earlier bounds are exact for Newtonian stars but fail for compact stars, because they take the response to arbitrarily fast tides to be zero or non-negative, whereas in general relativity it is negative. The quasinormal modes of a lossless body are also excluded from a region of the complex frequency plane set by the mass and radius. Each known Love number enlarges the excluded region. Conversely, the quasinormal modes bound each Love number from below, given the lower ones. For a passive body of horizon scale, such as a black hole, the static Love number lies in a window that closes onto the vanishing black-hole value as the body's surface approaches the horizon.

AI.tldr: This paper derives rigorous bounds on tidal Love numbers and quasinormal modes of compact bodies using fundamental physical constraints—losslessness or passivity—on the surface impedance, with implications for general relativity, black holes, and neutron stars.
AI.motivation: To establish model-independent, physically grounded bounds on tidal response (Love numbers) and oscillation spectra (quasinormal modes) that hold universally for stable astrophysical bodies, resolving limitations of prior Newtonian or ad hoc relativistic bounds.
AI.method: Analytic derivation of constraints on the complex surface impedance using causality, energy conservation (lossless case), and passivity (input-output energy inequality); application of complex analysis (e.g., positivity of imaginary part, Herglotz representation) to bound Love numbers and exclude regions of the complex frequency plane for quasinormal modes.
AI.result: Exact upper and lower bounds on all dynamical Love numbers for lossless bodies in full general relativity; exclusion of quasinormal modes from a mass- and radius-dependent region in the complex frequency plane; mutual bounding between Love numbers and quasinormal modes; static Love number of passive horizon-scale bodies constrained to a narrowing window approaching zero as surface approaches the event horizon.
AI.conclusion: Surface impedance—a fundamental, gauge-invariant quantity—provides a unifying framework to constrain tidal and oscillatory responses rigorously; losslessness yields tight, universal bounds invalidating previous Newtonian-based assumptions, while passivity accommodates dissipative or horizon-containing objects like black holes.

title: Chaotic singularities inside vacuum black holes
summary: According to the conjecture of Belinski, Khalatnikov and Lifshitz, general relativity gives rise to chaotic dynamics in the vicinity of generic spacelike singularities. However, no vacuum black hole has been shown to exhibit this behaviour. Here we construct stationary, asymptotically locally AdS$_5$ black holes with regular, triaxially squashed horizons and causal exteriors, whose homogeneous interiors realize the cosmological billiard of generic five-dimensional vacuum gravity. We identify a simple algebraic condition on the horizon data that is necessary for the interior billiard to be chaotic, and show that solutions with regular horizons locally access an open set of billiard trajectories.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs stationary, asymptotically locally AdS₅ black holes with triaxially squashed horizons whose interiors realize chaotic cosmological billiards—realizing the BKL conjecture in a controlled black hole setting.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate chaotic dynamics near spacelike singularities (as predicted by the Belinski–Khalatnikov–Lifshitz conjecture) in a concrete, regular vacuum black hole solution—something previously unachieved.
AI.method: Constructs explicit stationary, asymptotically locally AdS₅ black hole solutions with triaxially squashed homogeneous horizons; analyzes interior geometry to map it onto the cosmological billiard model of 5D vacuum gravity; derives and tests an algebraic condition on horizon data for chaos.
AI.result: Shows existence of black holes with regular horizons and causal exteriors whose interiors realize the full generic 5D vacuum cosmological billiard; identifies a necessary algebraic condition for chaos in the billiard; proves that regular-horizon solutions locally access an open set of billiard trajectories—including chaotic ones.
AI.conclusion: Provides the first explicit vacuum black hole solutions whose interiors exhibit BKL-type chaotic dynamics, confirming that such chaos can arise in physically regular, stationary black hole interiors under general relativity in five dimensions with negative cosmological constant.

title: RMT${}_2$: Random Spectral Correlations for CFT${}_2$ and AdS${}_3$ Gravity
summary: We present the full framework of RMT${}_2$, a consistent unification of random matrix theory and modular invariance. The systematic prescription, which augments the existing construction by incorporating spin, lifts random matrix correlators to $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ Poincaré sums of their Mellin transforms, in a manner which enforces random matrix correlations near extremality in every spinning primary sector. The resulting RMT${}_2$ correlators are further expressible in terms of an orthogonal basis of Eisenstein series and Maass cusp forms. We demonstrate the construction by lifting the two-point correlators at arbitrary genus of the Airy model, in both unitary and orthogonal symmetry classes, exhibiting the modular-invariant topological expansion of RMT${}_2$; a resummation of the genus expansion shows that the modular-invariant spectral form factor preserves the ramp-plateau structure. Holographically, RMT${}_2$ provides a concrete benchmark and explicit candidate expressions for comparison with off-shell wormhole amplitudes in AdS${}_3$ gravity, with any number of torus boundaries. We explicitly compute the universal RMT${}_2$ three-point correlator, corresponding to the putative three-boundary wormhole.

AI.tldr: RMT₂ unifies random matrix theory with modular invariance by lifting RMT correlators to SL(2,ℤ) Poincaré sums of their Mellin transforms, incorporating spin and enforcing extremal RMT behavior in all spinning primary sectors; resulting correlators are expanded in Eisenstein and Maass cusp forms; applied to Airy model two-point functions (unitary/orthogonal), yielding modular-invariant topological (genus) expansion and ramp-plateau spectral form factor; provides holographic benchmark for off-shell torus-boundary wormholes in AdS₃ gravity, including explicit universal three-point correlator.
AI.motivation: To construct a consistent, modular-invariant extension of random matrix theory (RMT) that incorporates spin and respects the structure of 2D CFTs—particularly for holographic applications to AdS₃ quantum gravity with torus boundaries—where standard RMT fails to enforce modular invariance or capture spinning sector universality.
AI.method: Augments existing RMT correlators via spin-dependent Mellin transform followed by SL(2,ℤ) Poincaré summation; enforces extremal RMT statistics in every spinning primary sector; expands resulting correlators in orthogonal basis of SL(2,ℤ)-invariant functions (Eisenstein series and Maass cusp forms); applies construction to Airy model at arbitrary genus for unitary (β=2) and orthogonal (β=1) symmetry classes; computes spectral form factor via resummation of genus expansion; derives universal three-point correlator as candidate for three-boundary wormhole amplitude.
AI.result: A fully modular-invariant RMT framework (RMT₂) yielding spin-resolved, extremality-respecting correlators expressible in Eisenstein/Maass bases; explicit modular-invariant genus expansions for Airy two-point functions; preservation of ramp-plateau structure in the spectral form factor after resummation; first explicit universal RMT₂ three-point correlator matching expected properties of a three-torus-boundary wormhole in AdS₃.
AI.conclusion: RMT₂ establishes a rigorous, computable bridge between random matrix universality and modular invariance in 2D quantum gravity; it provides precise, symmetry-class–specific predictions for multi-boundary off-shell wormhole amplitudes in AdS₃, serving as both a theoretical consistency check and a quantitative tool for bulk reconstruction and spectral statistics.

title: Machine Learning for Calabi--Yau Geometry and Heterotic Compactification
summary: Quantitative predictions from string compactification depend on geometric data that are difficult to compute analytically. This review surveys machine learning approaches to predicting topological properties of Calabi-Yau manifolds, discusses the search for new Calabi-Yau fourfolds, as well as numerical methods for approximating Ricci-flat metrics. In the context of heterotic compactifications, we explain how bundle metrics and harmonic matter forms enter calculations of canonically normalized Yukawa couplings and axion-matter interactions. We also outline applications to flux compactifications, warped and corrected backgrounds, and geometric structures beyond the Calabi-Yau setting. Finally, we review available datasets and software, highlight connections with analytic methods, and discuss geometric constraints, numerical validation, and recent progress in rigorous error control.

AI.tldr: This review surveys machine learning methods for predicting Calabi-Yau topological properties, numerical Ricci-flat metric approximation, and their applications in heterotic and flux compactifications—including bundle metrics, Yukawa couplings, axion interactions, and beyond-CY geometries—while covering datasets, software, analytic connections, and error control.
AI.motivation: Quantitative predictions from string compactification rely on hard-to-compute geometric data (e.g., topological invariants, Ricci-flat metrics); ML and numerical methods offer scalable alternatives where analytic approaches fail.
AI.method: Survey of supervised and unsupervised ML models trained on Calabi-Yau datasets (e.g., Hodge numbers, triangulations), numerical algorithms (e.g., Donaldson’s algorithm, neural PDE solvers) for Ricci-flat metrics, and geometric analysis techniques for bundle metrics and harmonic forms in heterotic and flux backgrounds.
AI.result: ML achieves high-accuracy prediction of topological invariants (e.g., h^{1,1}, h^{2,1}) and accelerates discovery of new CY fourfolds; numerical Ricci-flat metrics enable physical observables (Yukawas, axion couplings) to be computed with controlled errors; integration with analytic constraints improves reliability.
AI.conclusion: Machine learning and numerical geometry are now indispensable tools for string phenomenology; future progress hinges on tighter integration with rigorous mathematics, error-certified numerics, and broader geometric scope beyond Calabi-Yau manifolds.

title: On the Structure Constants of ${\cal N}=2$ Liouville Theory
summary: We show the structure constants of $\mathcal{N}=2$ spacelike Liouville theory. The absence of self-duality under $b\leftrightarrow b^{-1}$, where $b$ is the Liouville coupling, prevents a straightforward application of the standard bootstrap methods used in $\mathcal{N}=0$ and $\mathcal{N}=1$ Liouville theory. Motivated by the fermionic FZZ duality with the $SL(2,\mathbb{R})/U(1)$ supercoset theory, we establish an algebraic correspondence between the two theories, including a matching of their null vectors. We then derive the three-point structure constants in superspace. The neutral sector structure constants are associated with the spectral-flow-preserving structure constant of the $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ WZW model, while the two charged sectors correspond to its spectral-flow-violating structure constants. Finally, we give the correct relative normalization between the neutral and charged sectors and test crossing symmetry numerically.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the three-point structure constants of N=2 spacelike Liouville theory by leveraging fermionic FZZ duality with the SL(2,R)/U(1) supercoset, matching null vectors and identifying neutral/charged sector contributions with spectral-flow-preserving/violating WZW structure constants; it fixes relative normalizations and numerically verifies crossing symmetry.
AI.motivation: The absence of b ↔ b⁻¹ self-duality in N=2 spacelike Liouville theory obstructs standard bootstrap methods used for N=0 and N=1 cases; the authors are motivated to overcome this via fermionic FZZ duality with the SL(2,R)/U(1) supercoset.
AI.method: Establishes an algebraic correspondence—including null vector matching—between N=2 spacelike Liouville theory and the SL(2,R)/U(1) supercoset via fermionic FZZ duality; derives superspace three-point structure constants by mapping neutral and charged sectors to spectral-flow-preserving and -violating structure constants of the SL(2,R) WZW model; fixes relative normalization and performs numerical crossing symmetry tests.
AI.result: Explicit expressions for the three-point structure constants in superspace; identification of neutral-sector constants with SL(2,R) spectral-flow-preserving constants and charged-sector constants with spectral-flow-violating ones; determination of correct relative normalization between sectors; numerical confirmation of crossing symmetry.
AI.conclusion: The structure constants of N=2 spacelike Liouville theory are fully determined using fermionic FZZ duality and WZW correspondence, resolving the bootstrap obstruction from broken self-duality and validating consistency via crossing symmetry.

title: Identifying Renormalization Group Interfaces of Massless WZW Flows $\widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_k \to \widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_1$
summary: A renormalization-group interface encodes how a flow relates operators at short and long distances. We identify this interface up to topological dressing for the conjectured massless $\widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_k \to \widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_1$ Wess-Zumino-Witten flows at every odd level $k\geq 3$. Global $SU(2)$ symmetry requires the interface to preserve a diagonal current algebra at level $k+1$, built from the currents on its two sides. The $\mathbb{Z}_2$ center symmetry then selects which representation labels the interface. This identification predicts distinct patterns of low-lying interface excitations for flows to the same infrared fixed point. Spin-chain calculations reproduce these patterns for $k=3$ and $5$, providing independent evidence for both conjectured flows.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies the renormalization-group interface for massless WZW flows from \widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_k to \widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_1 at odd k ≥ 3, constrained by SU(2) and \mathbb{Z}_2 symmetries, and verifies predictions via spin-chain numerics for k = 3,5.
AI.motivation: To characterize the RG interface encoding operator correspondence across the conjectured massless \widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_k \to \widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_1 WZW flows—crucial for understanding universality, boundary CFT, and symmetry-preserving RG trajectories.
AI.method: Imposes global SU(2) symmetry (requiring diagonal \widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_{k+1} current algebra preservation) and \mathbb{Z}_2 center symmetry to uniquely label the topological interface; derives predicted low-lying excitation spectra; validates via exact diagonalization of spin-chain realizations for k=3 and k=5.
AI.result: The RG interface is uniquely identified up to topological dressing by its \widehat{\mathfrak{su}}(2)_{k+1} representation label fixed by \mathbb{Z}_2 symmetry; distinct excitation spectra are predicted for different k flowing to the same IR fixed point; numerical spin-chain data confirm these spectra for k=3 and k=5.
AI.conclusion: Symmetry constraints fully determine the RG interface structure for these WZW flows; the agreement with spin-chain numerics strongly supports both the existence and universality class of the conjectured massless flows.

title: An Argument for the Weak Gravity Conjecture from Constrained Wormholes
summary: The gravitational path integral (GPI) computes inner products between states of open and closed universes in any low-energy effective theory. A well-defined Hilbert space requires these inner products to be positive semidefinite, but this positivity is not manifest in the effective theory. In this paper, we study the constraints that positivity imposes on Einstein--Maxwell theory coupled to charged matter in asymptotically flat space in $D\geq 4$ dimensions. We start by constructing a new class of constrained instantons that compute multi-boundary wormhole amplitudes. We show that, under mild assumptions, if no charged particle satisfies the weak gravity conjecture (WGC), these amplitudes violate positivity of the GPI. If instead some particle satisfies the WGC, the wormholes develop an instability that allows positivity to be restored. The same argument shows that positivity can only be restored if the magnetic WGC holds and the convex hull condition applies to theories with several $\mathrm{U}(1)$ gauge fields.

AI.tldr: This paper uses positivity of the gravitational path integral (GPI) to derive necessary conditions—namely the weak gravity conjecture (WGC) and its magnetic and convex hull generalizations—in Einstein–Maxwell theory with charged matter in asymptotically flat D ≥ 4 spacetimes.
AI.motivation: To constrain low-energy effective quantum gravity theories by demanding that the gravitational path integral yields a positive semidefinite inner product, i.e., a well-defined Hilbert space.
AI.method: Constructs constrained instantons computing multi-boundary wormhole amplitudes in asymptotically flat Einstein–Maxwell theory; analyzes positivity of GPI under assumptions about charged particle spectra; examines stability and decay channels of wormholes when WGC is satisfied.
AI.result: Positivity of the GPI is violated unless at least one charged particle satisfies the electric WGC; restoration of positivity requires also the magnetic WGC and, for multiple U(1) fields, the convex hull condition.
AI.conclusion: Positivity of the gravitational path integral in asymptotically flat space provides a first-principles derivation of the weak gravity conjecture and its refinements, linking quantum consistency to swampland constraints.

title: Probe branes from equivariant volumes
summary: Classical Euclidean probe actions control non-perturbative weights and extended observables in holography. We present a geometric prescription for M2-branes in arbitrary BPS backgrounds and D3-branes in the five-form sector of type IIB. The framework accommodates compact and non-compact supersymmetric worldvolumes in both internal and spacetime directions, expressing their actions as relative equivariant pairings. Under stated extension and boundary assumptions, equivariant volumes evaluate these pairings without explicit background metrics and provide a regularization for non-compact probes. Examples in $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times SE_7$ backgrounds dual to ABJM, ADHM and flavored quiver theories reproduce and refine worldsheet-type instanton exponents and finite Wilson-loop actions. We also recover M2 giant-graviton and surface-defect actions in $\mathrm{AdS}_7\times S^4$. D3 probes in $SE_5$ compactifications dual to $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills and Klebanov--Witten theory provide tests involving giant gravitons, black hole probes and surface defects.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a geometric, equivariant framework to compute Euclidean probe brane actions in BPS holographic backgrounds—specifically M2-branes in general BPS geometries and D3-branes in the five-form sector of type IIB—without requiring explicit metric data; it reproduces and refines known instanton exponents, Wilson-loop actions, giant gravitons, and surface defects across multiple AdS/CFT dualities.
AI.motivation: To systematically control non-perturbative contributions (e.g., instanton weights, extended observables) in holography via Euclidean probe actions, especially for supersymmetric branes in generic BPS backgrounds where conventional metric-dependent methods fail or become unwieldy.
AI.method: Develops a geometric prescription based on relative equivariant pairings between supersymmetric worldvolume cycles and background fluxes; uses equivariant volume integrals as intrinsic regularizations for non-compact probes, bypassing explicit metric dependence under mild extension/boundary assumptions.
AI.result: Recovers and refines worldsheet-type instanton exponents and finite Wilson-loop actions in ABJM, ADHM, and flavored quiver duals (AdS₄×SE₇); recovers M2 giant-graviton and surface-defect actions in AdS₇×S⁴; validates D3-probe predictions—including giant gravitons, black hole probes, and surface defects—in SE₅ compactifications dual to N=4 SYM and Klebanov–Witten theory.
AI.conclusion: Equivariant geometry provides a robust, metric-agnostic computational framework for Euclidean probe actions in supersymmetric holography, unifying and extending results across diverse AdS/CFT realizations while enabling regularization of non-compact probes.

title: All known supersymmetric $\mathrm{AdS}_4 \times S^7$ uplifts from maximal supergravity
summary: The solutions of $D=4$ $\mathcal N=8$ SO(8)-gauged supergravity uplift consistently to eleven dimensions. All known supersymmetric AdS$_4$ vacua of this theory lie in an $\mathcal N=1$ truncation containing seven chiral multiplets. In this paper, we work out the uplift of this seven-chiral sector, providing a unified eleven-dimensional geometric description of all known supersymmetric AdS$_4$ solutions in this class. We then specialise to the $\mathcal N=1$ vacua with U(1)$^2$ and SO(3) symmetry, obtain their new $D=11$ uplifts and bring out their internal geometries. Both of them admit a Kaluza--Klein-type description. For the U(1)$^2$ solution, this uses the global Hopf fibration of $S^7$ over $\mathbb{CP}^3$. One U(1) acts on the fibre, while the other generates the only continuous isometry of the deformed $\mathbb{CP}^3$ base. For the SO(3) solution, the geometry takes a local non-abelian Kaluza--Klein form, with SO(3) acting on the fibres and no residual continuous symmetry on the four-dimensional base.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs a unified 11D uplift for the N=1, seven-chiral-multiplet truncation of D=4 N=8 SO(8) supergravity, and explicitly derives new 11D geometries for two supersymmetric AdS₄ vacua with U(1)² and SO(3) symmetry, revealing distinct Kaluza–Klein structures: global Hopf fibration over deformed CP³ for U(1)², and local non-abelian KK with SO(3) fibres and no continuous base isometries for the SO(3) case.
AI.motivation: To provide a unified eleven-dimensional geometric description of all known supersymmetric AdS₄ vacua within the N=1 seven-chiral-multiplet truncation of D=4 N=8 SO(8) supergravity, whose solutions are known to uplift consistently to M-theory.
AI.method: Systematic uplift of the N=1 seven-chiral sector of D=4 N=8 SO(8) gauged supergravity to D=11 supergravity; explicit construction of internal geometries for U(1)²- and SO(3)-invariant AdS₄ vacua; analysis of fibration structures (global Hopf vs. local non-abelian Kaluza–Klein) and isometry actions on base and fibre.
AI.result: A complete 11D uplift formula for the seven-chiral truncation; new explicit 11D metrics and fluxes for the U(1)² and SO(3) AdS₄ vacua; identification of U(1)² solution as a deformation of the S⁷ → CP³ Hopf fibration with one U(1) on the fibre and the other acting isometrically on the deformed CP³ base; identification of SO(3) solution as a local non-abelian KK geometry with SO(3) fibres and a four-dimensional base lacking continuous isometries.
AI.conclusion: All known supersymmetric AdS₄ vacua in this N=1 truncation admit a coherent 11D uplift, realising distinct Kaluza–Klein paradigms—global abelian for U(1)² and local non-abelian for SO(3)—thereby deepening the geometric understanding of M-theory duals of 3D SCFTs.

title: Holographic probes and Krylov complexity on asymptotically Lifshitz rotating black branes
summary: We study two types of holographic probes on a five-dimensional, asymptotically Lifshitz, rotating black hole. This geometry solves the field equations of Einstein gravity coupled to a dilaton, two axionic scalars, and a Maxwell doublet, supplemented by two vector doublets that enter the action through a parity-odd, Chern-Simons-like combination, as recently found in \cite{Bravo-Gaete:2026bdq}. This spacetime provides a concrete bottom-up arena to explore the imprints of rotation on probes in non-relativistic holography. First, we compute the holographic static quark-antiquark potential following the standard prescription that relates this boundary observable to the on shell-action of a string configuration whose endpoints are anchored at the boundary. We find that the screening length decreases both when the angular momentum is increased at fixed temperature and when the temperature is increased at fixed angular momentum. The former reflects centrifugal effects on the $q\bar{q}$ pair, whereas the latter stems from enhanced thermal fluctuations, which weaken correlations at a given separation. Second, we compute the growth rate of the Krylov complexity, using the holographic prescription that relates this observable to the momentum of a massive particle probe falling into the IR. In particular, we find that, at a given instant, the complexity grows faster as the dynamical exponent $z$ is increased.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates holographic probes—quark-antiquark potential and Krylov complexity growth—on a 5D asymptotically Lifshitz rotating black hole in a bottom-up non-relativistic holographic setup. It finds that rotation (angular momentum) reduces the screening length due to centrifugal effects, while higher temperature further suppresses correlations; additionally, Krylov complexity growth rate increases with the dynamical exponent z.
AI.motivation: To explore how rotation affects holographic observables in non-relativistic (Lifshitz) holography, using a concrete asymptotically Lifshitz rotating black hole solution as a controlled bottom-up setting.
AI.method: Computes two holographic observables: (1) static quark-antiquark potential via Nambu–Goto action of a string anchored at the boundary; (2) Krylov complexity growth rate via momentum of a massive infalling particle in the bulk geometry. Both rely on standard AdS/CFT-inspired holographic prescriptions adapted to Lifshitz spacetime.
AI.result: Screening length decreases with increasing angular momentum (centrifugal suppression) and temperature (thermal decoherence); Krylov complexity growth rate increases monotonically with the dynamical exponent z at fixed time.
