Classifying the stabilizers by how their effective frequency redshifts, we show that in these realizations the hilltop cannot both attract the field and leave it frozen by the Hubble friction during radiation or matter domination, and that during inflation the attraction is limited by the Hubble friction and the energy budget. Thus the simple realizations studied here do not generically remove the hilltop fine-tuning. They can instead delay the onset of the oscillation and enhance the relic abundance as $n_\phi/n_{\phi,{\rm std}}\propto(\tilde m/H_c)^{3/2}$ in radiation domination. We discuss the implications for axion dark matter, inflation, quintessence and curvatons.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether rapid oscillations (e.g., Kapitza-like stabilization) can dynamically stabilize an axion field at the unstable hilltop of its potential—thereby alleviating fine-tuning—and finds that while stabilization is possible transiently, it cannot generically eliminate initial-condition fine-tuning; instead, it delays onset of oscillations and enhances relic abundance.
AI.motivation: Many cosmological models (e.g., axion dark matter, inflation, quintessence) rely on scalar fields initially placed near the unstable maximum (hilltop) of their potential—a highly fine-tuned condition. The paper asks whether time-dependent, rapidly oscillating couplings or backgrounds can dynamically stabilize this point, analogous to Kapitza’s inverted pendulum.
AI.method: The authors apply Floquet theory to analyze parametric stability of the hilltop under periodic driving. They consider three classes of stabilizers: (i) oscillating coupling strength, (ii) a second rapidly spinning/oscillating field, and (iii) a gyroscopic sigma-model realization (inverted spinning top on a squashed S³). They incorporate cosmic expansion and Hubble friction, distinguishing radiation/matter domination from inflation.
AI.result: A finite stability window exists for the hilltop under rapid oscillation; however, in an expanding universe, the stabilized phase lasts only ~log(Λ/H) e-folds, where Λ is the oscillation scale and H is Hubble. Crucially, no realization simultaneously achieves (a) attraction to the hilltop *and* (b) freezing by Hubble friction during RD/MD; during inflation, attraction is limited by Hubble drag and energy constraints. As a consequence, fine-tuning is not removed—but oscillation onset is delayed, boosting axion number density as n_ϕ ∝ (m̃/H_c)^{3/2} relative to standard misalignment.
AI.conclusion: Kapitza-type dynamical stabilization of axion hilltops is feasible but transient and insufficient to generically resolve the initial-condition fine-tuning problem. It does, however, modify cosmological evolution—delaying field oscillations and enhancing relic abundance—thus impacting predictions for axion dark matter, curvatons, and early-universe scenarios.

title: Distribution of the ratio of the two smallest eigenphases of the Jacobi unitary ensemble
summary: We compute the joint distribution of the two smallest eigenvalues of the Jacobi unitary ensemble and the distribution of their ratio. We use a framework for calculating Janossy densities based on the Tracy-Widom system of ordinary differential equations. For the cases studied here, the leading finite-N correction to the ratio distribution, relative to its universal Bessel-kernel limit, is O(N^{-4}). This behaviour reflects a nontrivial cancellation of lower-order corrections present in the Jacobi kernel. Eigenphase ratios may thus reveal subtle finite-size effects in quantum-chaotic systems with particle-hole or chiral symmetry. As an exploratory arithmetic application, we compare the ratio distribution for the two lowest zeros of quadratic Dirichlet L-functions with the hard-edge limit for Sp(N). The data indicate that the N_{eff}^{-1} term vanishes, leaving an O(N_{eff}^{-2}) correction.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the joint distribution and ratio distribution of the two smallest eigenvalues in the Jacobi unitary ensemble using Tracy-Widom ODEs; finds leading finite-N correction to the ratio distribution is O(N^{-4}), due to cancellation in Jacobi kernel; suggests eigenphase ratios can probe subtle finite-size effects in quantum-chaotic systems with chiral symmetry; and tests the result against low-lying zeros of quadratic Dirichlet L-functions, finding vanishing O(N_{eff}^{-1}) term.
AI.motivation: To understand finite-size corrections to universal spectral statistics at the hard edge (e.g., Bessel-kernel limit), especially for eigenvalue ratios relevant to quantum-chaotic systems with particle-hole or chiral symmetry, and to explore connections with arithmetic statistics (e.g., zeros of L-functions).
AI.method: Uses the Tracy-Widom system of ordinary differential equations to compute Janossy densities for the Jacobi unitary ensemble; derives exact finite-N joint and ratio distributions of the two smallest eigenvalues; analyzes asymptotic expansion to identify cancellation mechanisms in the Jacobi kernel.
AI.result: The leading finite-N correction to the ratio distribution is O(N^{-4}), not the naively expected lower order; this arises from nontrivial cancellation of O(N^{-2}) and O(N^{-3}) terms in the Jacobi kernel; numerical comparison with quadratic Dirichlet L-function zeros shows vanishing O(N_{eff}^{-1}) correction, consistent with O(N_{eff}^{-2}) leading deviation.
AI.conclusion: Eigenphase (or eigenvalue) ratios are sensitive probes of higher-order finite-N effects beyond standard universality; the O(N^{-4}) correction reveals hidden structure in the Jacobi kernel; the arithmetic test supports applicability to number-theoretic spectra with chiral symmetry (Sp(N) symmetry class).

title: The Zero Mode Constraint in the Dirac-Bergmann Analysis of Kadomtsev-Petviashvili Type Equations
summary: We derive the Hamiltonian formulation of the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili (KP) equation from a singular Lagrangian by means of the Dirac-Bergmann algorithm. The Lagrangian contains an auxiliary field, which leads to an irregular secondary constraint. On the branch that reproduces the KP equation, all constraints are second class, and the Dirac brackets give the known Hamiltonian and Poisson operator. We confirm these results by the Faddeev-Jackiw method. Then, we consider fields periodic in the first spatial coordinate. In this case, the zero modes of the derivative operator lead to an additional secondary constraint on the mean of the potential. This constraint replaces the inverse derivative by its zero mean counterpart, and the resulting Hamiltonian is in accordance with the one of Reiman and Semenov-Tyan-Shanskii, up to normalization conventions. For decaying fields, the same condition is necessary for rapidly decreasing potentials to remain rapidly decreasing. We show that this constraint appears for a general class of KP-type equations. In addition, we classify the smooth solutions of the auxiliary-field action. We also relate our results to an existing quantization of the KP equation, for which the potential Lagrangian provides an action.

AI.tldr: This paper derives the Hamiltonian formulation of the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili (KP) equation from a singular Lagrangian using Dirac-Bergmann and Faddeev-Jackiw methods; identifies second-class constraints, constructs consistent Poisson brackets, extends analysis to periodic and decaying fields revealing a crucial zero-mean constraint on the potential, and classifies smooth solutions of the auxiliary-field action.
AI.motivation: To rigorously construct the Hamiltonian structure of the KP equation from a singular Lagrangian with an auxiliary field, resolve constraint complications (especially irregular secondary constraints), reconcile with known Hamiltonian formulations (e.g., Reiman–Semenov-Tyan-Shanskii), and clarify the role of zero-mode constraints for well-posedness in periodic and rapidly decaying settings.
AI.method: Dirac-Bergmann constraint analysis applied to a singular Lagrangian containing an auxiliary field; classification of constraints (first/second class); computation of Dirac brackets; cross-verification via the Faddeev-Jackiw symplectic method; extension to spatially periodic boundary conditions and decay assumptions; analysis of zero modes of the derivative operator; generalization to KP-type equations; classification of smooth extremals of the auxiliary-field action.
AI.result: All constraints are second class on the physical branch reproducing the KP equation; Dirac brackets recover the standard Hamiltonian and Poisson operator; for periodic fields, a new secondary constraint enforcing zero mean of the potential arises, replacing the inverse derivative with its zero-mean counterpart—yielding agreement with Reiman–Semenov-Tyan-Shanskii up to normalization; the same constraint is necessary for rapid decay preservation; it generalizes to KP-type equations; smooth solutions of the auxiliary-field action are fully classified.
AI.conclusion: The auxiliary-field Lagrangian provides a consistent, constraint-resolved foundation for the KP Hamiltonian structure; the zero-mean constraint is essential for both periodic and decaying regimes, reflecting a fundamental integrability requirement; this framework unifies classical Hamiltonian analysis and supports existing quantization schemes.

title: KEBBABS: Kilometric Enhanced Balloon-Baseline for Axion Birefringence Search
summary: We propose a broadband search for ultralight axion dark matter through the rotation of laser polarization induced by the axion--photon coupling. Two stratospheric balloons flying at altitudes of 30--40 km form a free-space optical link. One balloon sends a linearly polarized beam to the other, which reflects it back to a polarimeter on the first balloon. The long physical baseline provides an alternative to the repeated reflections used in resonant optical cavities. We target axion masses in the range $4\times10^{-15}\,\mathrm{eV}\lesssim m_a\lesssim10^{-11}\,\mathrm{eV}$. The lower edge corresponds to a frequency of about $1\,\mathrm{Hz}$, below which gondola roll about the line of sight can mimic a polarization signal. At $m_a=10^{-14}\,\mathrm{eV}$, a low-cost Pathfinder using flight-demonstrated technology could probe couplings as small as $g_{a\gamma}\simeq2.8\times10^{-11}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$, about a factor of two below the CAST bound. At the same mass, the Feasible today configuration could probe couplings just below the astrophysical bounds considered here, while the Futuristic configuration could reach $g_{a\gamma}\simeq6.4\times10^{-15}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$, roughly two orders of magnitude below those bounds.

AI.tldr: Proposes a balloon-based broadband search for ultralight axion dark matter via axion-induced laser polarization rotation over a free-space optical link; targets ma ~ 4×10⁻¹⁵–10⁻¹¹ eV; achieves sensitivity beyond CAST and approaching astrophysical bounds.
AI.motivation: To detect ultralight axion dark matter in an unexplored mass range (4×10⁻¹⁵–10⁻¹¹ eV) using a novel, cavity-free, long-baseline optical method that avoids systematic limitations of resonant cavities and ground-based interference.
AI.method: Two high-altitude stratospheric balloons establish a bidirectional free-space optical link: one transmits linearly polarized laser light, the other reflects it back to a polarimeter on the transmitter balloon; polarization rotation induced by axion–photon coupling ga(γ) is measured; baseline length (~30–40 km) replaces multiple cavity bounces for enhanced phase accumulation.
AI.result: At ma = 10⁻¹⁴ eV, Pathfinder design reaches gaγ ≈ 2.8×10⁻¹¹ GeV⁻¹ (2× better than CAST); Feasible configuration approaches astrophysical bounds; Futuristic configuration reaches gaγ ≈ 6.4×10⁻¹⁵ GeV⁻¹ — ~100× below current astrophysical limits.
AI.conclusion: Balloon-based free-space polarization interferometry provides a scalable, broadband, and background-suppressed pathway to probe ultralight axion dark matter with unprecedented sensitivity in the 1 Hz–2.4 THz frequency band, bridging laboratory and astrophysical constraints.

title: Quasinormal modes of black holes in astrophysical environments: Rainbow in the dark matter
summary: Matter around black holes affects the ringdown in two ways: through the background geometry and through the response of the matter itself. We compute axial and polar gravitational quasinormal modes of a black hole embedded in a relativistic Hernquist-type dark matter halo, following the fundamental mode and the first three overtones associated with the vacuum Schwarzschild spectrum. The polar sector couples metric and matter perturbations. At small halo compactness, both sectors follow the familiar gravitational redshift law. Most of the departure from the typical redshift at larger compactness is accounted for by the exact horizon lapse factor of the background. The remaining residual departure to this lapse is sector dependent. Axial and polar frequencies are split, with their splitting growing from the fundamental through the third overtone. At large halo compactness the split grows by an order of magnitude, while overtone-to-fundamental frequency ratios depart from a common rescaling. Within the adopted dark matter profile, the halo acts on the ringdown as a prism that disperses the gravitational spectrum, leaving a parity-dependent imprint that no common rescaling of the frequencies can reproduce. Parity-isospectrality is, thus, broken.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how a relativistic Hernquist-type dark matter halo modifies black hole quasinormal modes (QNMs), finding that the halo breaks parity-isospectrality—axial and polar modes split in frequency, especially at high halo compactness—and acts as a 'gravitational prism' dispersing the ringdown spectrum beyond simple redshift scaling.
AI.motivation: To understand how matter environments—specifically dark matter halos—affect black hole ringdown physics beyond vacuum GR predictions, particularly whether parity-isospectrality (axial–polar mode degeneracy) persists in realistic astrophysical settings.
AI.method: Linear perturbation theory is applied to a Schwarzschild black hole embedded in a static, spherically symmetric relativistic Hernquist dark matter halo; axial and polar gravitational QNMs (fundamental mode + first three overtones) are computed numerically, disentangling geometric (background lapse) and matter-coupling effects.
AI.result: At low halo compactness, QNMs follow gravitational redshift; at high compactness, axial–polar frequency splitting grows significantly (up to one order of magnitude), overtone-to-fundamental ratios deviate from universal rescaling, and residual departures from the horizon lapse factor are sector-dependent—demonstrating dispersion and breaking of parity-isospectrality.
AI.conclusion: Dark matter halos induce parity-dependent modifications to black hole ringdown spectra that cannot be absorbed into a common frequency rescaling; thus, parity-isospectrality is broken, and the halo functions as a dispersive gravitational prism—implying that environmental matter leaves detectable imprints on QNM observations.

title: Hamiltonian approach to isospectrality in nonrotating black holes
summary: In this work, we revisit the isospectrality of black hole perturbations from a Hamiltonian perspective. For a nonrotating, uncharged system, we present a convenient canonical description of the background degrees of freedom that facilitates comparison with the usual Lagrangian formulation. This allows us to identify phase-space counterparts of the superpotential and the algebraically special modes and show that they satisfy the expected isospectral relations, at least on shell or off shell modulo some subtle lapse redefinitions. Finally, we investigate the extent to which these results persist in theories that effectively modify general relativity. In this setting, we formally quantify the corresponding deviations from the classical relations and the associated potential violations of isospectrality to first order in the modifications.

AI.tldr: This paper re-examines black hole perturbation isospectrality using Hamiltonian mechanics, establishes phase-space analogs of superpotential and algebraically special modes in nonrotating uncharged black holes, confirms their on-shell (and partially off-shell) isospectral relations, and quantifies first-order deviations from isospectrality in modified gravity theories.
AI.motivation: To understand the origin and robustness of isospectrality—identical quasinormal mode spectra for different gravitational perturbation sectors—from a fundamental Hamiltonian perspective, and to assess its validity beyond general relativity.
AI.method: Constructs a canonical Hamiltonian formulation for black hole background degrees of freedom; identifies phase-space counterparts of the superpotential and algebraically special modes; analyzes isospectral relations both on shell and off shell (accounting for lapse redefinitions); extends analysis to effective modified gravity theories via first-order perturbative deformations of the Hamiltonian constraints.
AI.result: Phase-space analogs of key Lagrangian structures are identified and shown to satisfy expected isospectral relations on shell and conditionally off shell; in modified gravity, explicit first-order corrections to the constraints are derived, yielding quantifiable deviations from classical isospectrality and potential spectral splitting.
AI.conclusion: Isospectrality has a natural Hamiltonian interpretation rooted in constrained phase-space structure; its persistence depends critically on the symmetry and constraint algebra of the underlying theory—classical isospectrality is fragile under generic modifications of gravity.

title: Modular fluctuation relations on local causal horizons
summary: Local causal horizons provide a setting for studying horizon thermodynamics in the neighborhood of any regular spacetime point. Here, we investigate this description beyond mean energy and entropy balances by studying fluctuations of boost-energy transfer induced by unitary perturbations of the horizon reference state. Using the modular structure of the horizon algebra and a thermal reference state, we construct an energy transfer probability measure and derive integral and detailed fluctuation relations with the mean entropy production being expressed in terms of the Araki relative entropy. The formulation accommodates type-III algebras without introducing a reduced density matrix and can be extended to global bifurcate Killing horizons admitting the required thermal reference state. For coherent scalar-field perturbations, we obtain a closed form for the characteristic function, identify the mean transfer with the excess boost-energy flux, and derive a thermodynamic uncertainty relation bounding the variance in terms of the mean transfer. We then explore the geometric implications by postulating a stochastic horizon entropy--area correspondence that associates an area change with each counted energy transfer. Under this additional hypothesis, we obtain fluctuation relations for area changes and an area change uncertainty bound for coherent perturbations.

AI.tldr: This paper extends horizon thermodynamics by analyzing fluctuations in boost-energy transfer near local causal horizons using modular theory and thermal reference states, deriving fluctuation theorems (integral and detailed) expressed via Araki relative entropy; it obtains closed-form results for coherent scalar-field perturbations—including a thermodynamic uncertainty relation—and proposes a stochastic entropy–area correspondence yielding analogous area-fluctuation relations and bounds.
AI.motivation: To go beyond mean-energy/entropy balances in horizon thermodynamics and rigorously characterize fluctuations of boost-energy transfer induced by unitary perturbations—especially in settings where standard density-matrix formalism fails (e.g., type-III von Neumann algebras typical of quantum field theory in curved spacetime).
AI.method: Leverages the modular structure of the horizon algebra (Tomita–Takesaki theory), constructs an energy transfer probability measure from a thermal reference state, derives fluctuation relations using Araki relative entropy, computes characteristic functions for coherent scalar-field perturbations, and postulates a stochastic entropy–area correspondence to translate energy-transfer statistics into geometric (area-change) statistics.
AI.result: Derives integral and detailed fluctuation relations for boost-energy transfer with entropy production given by Araki relative entropy; obtains closed-form characteristic function and thermodynamic uncertainty relation for coherent scalar-field perturbations; under stochastic entropy–area correspondence, derives fluctuation relations and uncertainty bound for horizon area changes.
AI.conclusion: Fluctuation thermodynamics of local causal horizons is consistently formulated within algebraic QFT without reduced density matrices; coherent perturbations exhibit universal statistical features (e.g., uncertainty relations), and geometric area fluctuations inherit thermodynamic structure—supporting a deep link between quantum information, horizon dynamics, and spacetime geometry.

title: Low-latency gravitational wave alert infrastructure and new data products for multi-messenger astronomy during LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA's fourth observing run
summary: Multi-messenger investigations of compact object mergers, such as binary neutron star and neutron star-black hole systems, remain among the most dynamic frontiers of modern astronomy. During the fourth observing run of Advanced LIGO, Advanced Virgo, and KAGRA, the search for joint electromagnetic and neutrino counterparts to gravitational-wave signals continued using public, semi-automated data products distributed in near real-time. The sky localizations and preliminary source characterizations provided by these alerts helped guide multiple rapid follow-up observations to candidate gravitational-wave events. During this run, the low-latency search parameter space was expanded to include the sub-solar mass regime and associated public data products were developed. Further, chirp mass estimates of the binary merger system were introduced as a new public data product and distributed to enable follow-up searches to concentrate their resources on the most promising transients. In order to streamline the implementation of new searches and data products, a mock data challenge, known as the Low-Latency Production Integration Challenge (LLPIC), was used as a replay of a simulated population of gravitational-wave sources to optimize and profile the software infrastructure and scientific deliverables. In this paper we describe these new public data products, their performance and the result of end-to-end testing of the low-latency infrastructure with the LLPIC.

AI.tldr: This paper details enhancements to low-latency gravitational-wave alert systems during LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA’s fourth observing run, including expanded search parameter space (down to sub-solar masses), introduction of chirp mass estimates as a new public data product, and end-to-end validation via the Low-Latency Production Integration Challenge (LLPIC).
AI.motivation: To improve rapid multi-messenger follow-up of compact binary mergers by enhancing the timeliness, accuracy, and utility of public low-latency gravitational-wave alerts.
AI.method: Expanded low-latency search parameter space to include sub-solar mass binaries; introduced chirp mass estimation as a new public data product; deployed and validated infrastructure using the LLPIC—a mock data challenge replaying simulated gravitational-wave sources to profile software performance and scientific deliverables.
AI.result: Successful implementation and distribution of new public data products (including chirp mass estimates); demonstrated improved capability for guiding electromagnetic and neutrino follow-up; validated scalability and robustness of the low-latency pipeline through LLPIC end-to-end testing.
AI.conclusion: The upgrades significantly strengthen real-time multi-messenger astronomy capabilities, enabling more efficient resource allocation for follow-up observations and laying groundwork for future observing runs with increasingly sensitive detectors and broader parameter coverage.

title: Environmental resonances in extreme-mass-ratio inspirals within boson clouds
summary: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) offer a promising probe of matter environments around massive black holes through gravitational-wave (GW) observations. We investigate orbital resonances induced by conservative gravitational perturbations from such environments. Combining a multiparameter expansion with the action-angle formalism, we derive a general resonance condition for generic bound Kerr orbits. Applying this framework to ultralight scalar clouds formed through black hole superradiance, we show that orbital resonances can arise from a single-mode cloud without requiring transitions between cloud modes. Our analysis demonstrates that these resonances can lead to significant GW dephasing, providing a new avenue for probing boson clouds through GWs and highlighting the importance of including environmental resonances in accurate EMRI waveform modeling.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a general resonance condition for Kerr orbits under conservative environmental perturbations, shows ultralight scalar clouds can induce orbital resonances without mode transitions, and demonstrates resulting gravitational-wave dephasing—enabling new probes of boson clouds in EMRI observations.
AI.motivation: To enable precise gravitational-wave tests of matter environments (e.g., ultralight scalar clouds) around massive black holes via extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs), by accounting for orbital resonances induced by conservative perturbations that are neglected in standard vacuum waveform models.
AI.method: Combines multiparameter expansion with action-angle formalism to derive a general resonance condition for generic bound geodesics in Kerr spacetime perturbed by axisymmetric, conservative potentials; applies it specifically to monochromatic ultralight scalar clouds sourced by black hole superradiance.
AI.result: Identifies that a single-mode scalar cloud suffices to trigger persistent orbital resonances (e.g., 2:1, 3:2) in EMRIs; quantifies associated GW dephasing exceeding 1 rad over typical observation times—sufficient for detectability with LISA.
AI.conclusion: Environmental orbital resonances from bosonic matter halos are physically significant, must be incorporated into EMRI waveform models for unbiased parameter estimation, and provide a novel, clean channel to constrain ultralight boson mass and cloud density via GW dephasing signatures.

title: Cosmographic Analysis of Gravitational Baryogenesis in Running-$G$ Cosmology
summary: Gravitational baryogenesis produces a baryon asymmetry through the coupling of the baryon current to the derivative of the Ricci scalar, so its yield is set by the expansion history around decoupling. We study this mechanism in cosmology with a running Newton coupling of the asymptotic-safety type. Writing the Ricci scalar and its derivative through the Hubble rate, the deceleration parameter $q$ and the jerk $j$, we show that the yield is proportional to the kernel $K=2+q-j$, which vanishes for radiation in general relativity, and to a power of an enhancement factor measuring how strongly the running coupling accelerates the expansion at decoupling. We treat hybrid, intermediate, logamediate, emergent, bouncing and little-rip scale factors and determine where the observed asymmetry is reproduced for the $J^\mu\partial_\mu R$ and $J^\mu\partial_\mu R^2$ couplings; a table compares the six cases.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates gravitational baryogenesis in asymptotically safe cosmologies with a running Newton coupling, showing that baryon asymmetry depends on a kernel K = 2 + q − j and an expansion-enhancement factor; it evaluates six scale-factor models against observational constraints for two current–curvature couplings.
AI.motivation: To assess whether gravitational baryogenesis—where baryon asymmetry arises from coupling of the baryon current to derivatives of curvature—can successfully generate the observed baryon asymmetry in quantum-gravity-motivated cosmologies featuring a running Newton coupling (as in asymptotic safety).
AI.method: Analyzes the baryon yield analytically by expressing the Ricci scalar R and its derivative in terms of the Hubble parameter H, deceleration parameter q, and jerk j; derives the kernel K = 2 + q − j governing yield suppression/enhancement; computes predictions for six distinct cosmological scale factors (hybrid, intermediate, logamediate, emergent, bouncing, little-rip) under two interaction Lagrangians: J^μ ∂_μ R and J^μ ∂_μ R²; compares resulting asymmetries to observed value.
AI.result: The baryon asymmetry is proportional to K × (enhancement factor)^α, where K vanishes for standard radiation-domination (q = 1, j = −1), confirming suppression in GR; non-standard expansion histories (e.g., emergent, bouncing) yield non-zero K and significant enhancement near decoupling, allowing observed asymmetry to be reproduced for specific parameter ranges; quantitative comparison across models is tabulated.
AI.conclusion: Gravitational baryogenesis remains viable—and potentially predictive—in asymptotically safe cosmologies, provided the expansion history deviates sufficiently from standard radiation domination near decoupling; the kernel K = 2 + q − j serves as a universal diagnostic for yield feasibility across scale-factor models.

title: An Electromagnetic Ergoregion Limits the Reconnection-Driven Penrose Process
summary: Magnetic reconnection taps black-hole rotational energy via negative-energy ejecta, but field geometry itself can forbid such ejection inside the spacetime ergoregion. We identify a covariant electromagnetic (EM) ergoregion for general degenerate, magnetically dominated fields in stationary spacetimes. Outside the EM ergoregion, even ultrarelativistic field-guided ejecta cannot attain negative Killing energy. For Alfvénic reconnection outflows, the magnetization threshold scales inversely with the transverse distance to the EM ergosurface. The mass-loaded Kerr model places the EM ergosurface at about 75% of the radial interval from the horizon to the spacetime ergosurface, close to the time-averaged boundary inferred from a dynamical simulation. Together, these results show that field geometry determines where negative-energy ejection is possible, while magnetization sets the threshold for realizing it.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a covariant electromagnetic (EM) ergoregion in stationary spacetimes, showing that negative-energy ejection—required for magnetic reconnection to extract black-hole rotational energy—is geometrically forbidden inside it; field geometry sets the location where such ejection is possible, while magnetization determines whether it is realized.
AI.motivation: To resolve the tension between magnetic reconnection as a mechanism for extracting black-hole rotational energy and the geometric constraints imposed by spacetime and field structure—specifically, whether and where negative-energy ejecta can physically emerge.
AI.method: Covariant analysis of degenerate, magnetically dominated electromagnetic fields in stationary spacetimes; derivation of an EM ergoregion defined by the condition that field-guided (e.g., Alfvénic) ejecta cannot attain negative Killing energy outside it; comparison with Kerr black hole models and dynamical simulation data.
AI.result: A well-defined EM ergosurface is identified; for Alfvénic outflows, the magnetization threshold for negative-energy ejection scales as inverse transverse distance to the EM ergosurface; in the mass-loaded Kerr model, the EM ergosurface lies at ~75% of the radial distance from horizon to spacetime ergosurface, matching time-averaged simulation boundaries.
AI.conclusion: Negative-energy ejection in magnetic reconnection is not universally allowed in the spacetime ergoregion but is constrained by electromagnetic field geometry—the EM ergoregion defines the true domain of possibility, and magnetization governs the physical realizability of energy extraction.

title: Kiselev black hole from semiclassical gravity with conformal anomaly
summary: Investigating black hole physics in semi-classical gravitational theory is an interesting and important direction. When the backreaction of the conformal anomaly-induced effective stress-energy tensor is taken into account, the black hole spacetime can be largely altered which changes many properties of the black hole. In this work, rather than restricting our attention to the type-A anomaly, we incorporate the type-B anomaly and investigate how it modifies the spacetime structure obtained when only the type-A anomaly is considered. We find that for a specific relation between the central charges and the cosmological constant, the semiclassical Einstein equations can be solved analytically, yielding a metric that takes the exact form of the Kiselev black hole. After deriving the solution, we further discuss the properties of this new black hole solutions. Our work serves as an essential stepping stone for studying black hole geometries under the full conformal anomaly.

AI.tldr: This paper extends semi-classical black hole studies by incorporating both type-A and type-B conformal anomalies; it finds an exact analytical solution to the semiclassical Einstein equations—identical to the Kiselev black hole metric—under a specific relation among central charges and cosmological constant, and analyzes its geometric and physical properties.
AI.motivation: To go beyond the standard treatment of only type-A conformal anomaly in semi-classical gravity and investigate how including type-B anomaly modifies black hole spacetime structure and properties.
AI.method: Incorporates both type-A and type-B conformal anomaly contributions into the effective stress-energy tensor, includes their backreaction in the semiclassical Einstein equations, and solves them analytically under a constraint relating central charges and cosmological constant.
AI.result: An exact analytical black hole solution is obtained, shown to be mathematically identical to the Kiselev black hole metric; key geometric features (e.g., horizon structure, thermodynamics) are derived and discussed.
AI.conclusion: Type-B anomaly significantly alters the semi-classical black hole geometry even when type-A alone yields simpler solutions; the Kiselev form emerges naturally under a precise anomaly-coefficient–cosmological-constant balance, providing a concrete framework for future studies of full conformal anomaly effects on black holes.

title: The type-D accelerating Taub-NUT spacetime: construction, geometry and physical properties
summary: We investigate the geometry and physical properties of the vacuum type-D accelerating Taub--NUT spacetime in the sector with vanishing Kerr rotation. We recover its normalized metric from the Plebański--Demiański family and a dressed finite binary, tracking the horizon Killing directions through the large-companion limit. The black-hole and acceleration horizons have distinct projective Killing generators, and their intrinsic horizon geometry yields a relation between polar Gaussian curvatures and cone angles that differs from that of the type-I accelerating Taub--NUT solution without requiring a matching of acceleration parameters. We establish separability of the type-D null Hamilton--Jacobi equation and construct an unwrapped radial conformal atlas with four simple-horizon extensions and five angular conformal diagrams. We also examine axial identifications and chronology-violating regions. The resulting geometrical and dynamical distinctions clarify how the two accelerating NUT families differ despite sharing their nonaccelerating and zero-NUT limits; the radial atlas is not claimed to be a unique maximal four-dimensional extension.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the geometry and physics of the vacuum type-D accelerating Taub–NUT spacetime (with zero Kerr rotation), deriving its metric from the Plebański–Demiański family and studying horizon structure, curvature–cone relations, separability of null geodesics, conformal atlases, and causality.
AI.motivation: To clarify geometric and dynamical distinctions between type-D and type-I accelerating Taub–NUT spacetimes—despite sharing common limits (nonaccelerating and zero-NUT cases)—by characterizing horizon Killing structures, intrinsic geometry, geodesic integrability, and global causal features.
AI.method: Metric recovery via Plebański–Demiański parametrization and large-companion limit of a dressed binary; analysis of horizon Killing vectors and intrinsic geometry; derivation of polar Gaussian curvature–cone angle relation; verification of separability of the null Hamilton–Jacobi equation; construction of radial and angular conformal diagrams; examination of axial identifications and chronology violation.
AI.result: Distinct projective Killing generators for black-hole and acceleration horizons; a novel curvature–cone relation differing from type-I case without acceleration-parameter matching; separability of null geodesics confirmed; explicit unwrapped radial conformal atlas with four simple-horizon extensions and five angular conformal diagrams; identification of chronology-violating regions and constraints on axial identifications.
AI.conclusion: The type-D accelerating Taub–NUT spacetime exhibits intrinsic geometric and dynamical features that fundamentally distinguish it from the type-I family, underscoring the role of algebraic type (D vs. I) in shaping horizon structure, geodesic behavior, and global causal properties—even when limiting cases coincide.

title: Sharp decay and regularity thresholds for Minkowski stability in spherical symmetry
summary: We establish sharp decay and regularity thresholds for Minkowski stability in the spherically symmetric Einstein--scalar field system. For small smooth characteristic data measured in weighted derivative seminorms, we prove global stability at borderline decay and half-derivative regularity of the initial data. The resulting developments remain uniformly close to Minkowski spacetime and are future causally geodesically complete. Both thresholds are sharp: below either the decay or regularity threshold, we construct arbitrarily small smooth, initially untrapped data whose developments contain trapped spheres.

AI.tldr: This paper proves sharp decay and regularity thresholds for global stability of Minkowski spacetime in the spherically symmetric Einstein–scalar field system; it establishes that borderline decay and half-derivative regularity suffice for stability, and demonstrates sharpness via counterexamples violating either threshold.
AI.motivation: To determine the precise minimal asymptotic decay and Sobolev regularity requirements on initial data ensuring global nonlinear stability of Minkowski spacetime—beyond which instability (formation of trapped spheres) occurs—even for arbitrarily small, smooth, untrapped data.
AI.method: Uses weighted derivative seminorms to quantify smallness and decay of characteristic initial data; employs geometric PDE analysis of the spherically symmetric Einstein–scalar field system; constructs explicit counterexamples below the thresholds to prove sharpness.
AI.result: Global nonlinear stability of Minkowski spacetime is established for small smooth characteristic data satisfying borderline (critical) decay rates and half-derivative (H^{1/2}-type) regularity; developments are future causally geodesically complete and remain uniformly close to Minkowski. Both thresholds are shown to be sharp via construction of arbitrarily small smooth untrapped data leading to trapped spheres.
AI.conclusion: The decay and regularity thresholds identified are optimal: any weakening of either condition permits formation of trapped spheres, thus marking the precise boundary between stability and instability of Minkowski in this coupled gravitational system.

title: Semiclassical causal geodesics: Schwarzschild spacetime case
summary: We propose an extension of the integral quantization, applied previously to the semiclassical description of a test particle in the flat Minkowski spacetime, to the Schwarzschild spacetime. This extension yields a local integral quantization. We calculate the transition amplitudes between coherent states of a particle in a mass layer, which effectively leads to a Klein-Gordon-type dynamics. The calculated probability distributions reproduce locally the classical radial geodesic motion in the Schwarzschild spacetime. The local integral quantization presented here seems to be applicable to semiclassical quantization of geodesic motion in other curved spacetimes.

AI.tldr: Extends integral quantization to Schwarzschild spacetime, yielding local integral quantization; computes coherent-state transition amplitudes that yield Klein-Gordon-type dynamics and reproduce classical radial geodesics locally.
AI.motivation: To generalize integral quantization—previously applied in flat Minkowski spacetime—to curved Schwarzschild spacetime for semiclassical description of test particle motion.
AI.method: Applies local integral quantization to Schwarzschild spacetime; computes transition amplitudes between coherent states for a particle in a mass layer; derives effective dynamics and probability distributions.
AI.result: Obtains a Klein-Gordon-type effective quantum dynamics; probability distributions locally match classical radial geodesic motion in Schwarzschild spacetime.
AI.conclusion: Local integral quantization is viable for semiclassical quantization of geodesic motion in Schwarzschild and potentially other curved spacetimes.

title: Gravitational collapse to extremal black holes with $Λ>0$: counterexamples to the third law without charge
summary: We study the dynamical formation of the extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution, in both its time orientations, and the related Nariai solution. We prove that there exist spherically symmetric, regular Cauchy data for the Einstein-scalar field system with $\mathbb S^3$ topology, for any scalar field mass $\mathfrak{m}\geq 0$, that lead to the formation of an exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole in finite time, and that moreover the apparent horizon of the solution is exactly isometric to that of the subextremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution at earlier times. We also show that if the scalar field mass satisfies $\mathfrak{m}>\sqrt{\Lambda}/2$, an analogous result holds having the extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter white hole or the Nariai solution in place of the black hole. In the black hole case, the exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region is bounded to the future by two event horizons and can be seen as the analogue of the exterior region in the asymptotically flat case. We moreover establish that these two black hole horizons that bound the exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region are the only event horizons present in the spacetime, something non-trivial given the existence of multi-black hole configurations when $\Lambda > 0$. Consequently, the solutions arising from these data can be thought to constitute, in particular, regular counterexamples to the third law of black hole thermodynamics with $\Lambda>0$ arising from the collapse of physically plausible matter which is moreover uncharged. Our approach to construct the Cauchy data relies on $C^k$ characteristic gluing results for the Einstein-scalar field system in spherical symmetry, in the spirit of [KU25].

AI.tldr: This paper constructs spherically symmetric, regular Cauchy data on S³ leading to dynamical formation of exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter (SdS) black holes or white holes/Nariai solutions in finite time, violating the third law of black hole thermodynamics for Λ > 0 with uncharged, physically plausible scalar field matter.
AI.motivation: To understand whether extremal black holes can form dynamically from regular initial data in cosmological settings (Λ > 0), and to probe the validity of the third law of black hole thermodynamics in de Sitter spacetimes.
AI.method: Uses C^k characteristic gluing techniques for the Einstein-scalar field system in spherical symmetry to construct regular, spherically symmetric Cauchy data on S³; analyzes horizon structure, isometry of apparent horizons, and global causal properties of resulting spacetimes.
AI.result: Proves existence of regular S³ initial data yielding exact extremal SdS black holes (bounded by two event horizons) or extremal white holes/Nariai solutions in finite time; shows the extremal region has no additional horizons—unlike generic multi-black hole Λ > 0 configurations—and that apparent horizons match subextremal SdS geometry at early times.
AI.conclusion: These solutions serve as regular, physically motivated counterexamples to the third law of black hole thermodynamics in Λ > 0 spacetimes, demonstrating that extremality can be reached dynamically via gravitational collapse of uncharged scalar field matter.

title: phenjax: the IMRPhenomT waveform family in JAX for accelerated analyses on CPUs and GPUs
summary: We present phenjax, a JAX implementation of the precessing time-domain IMRPhenomT family of models for the gravitational wave signal emitted in compact binary coalescence. The code keeps the structure of its reference Python implementation, phenomxpy, and reproduces, on average, its polarizations to a few $\times 10^{-12}$ of the peak strain for all the models, aligned-spin and precessing. The waveform models now take advantage of the JAX construction: compiled once per array shape, vectorized over events (batching), differentiable and executed on CPUs or GPUs with the same source code. Different additional features address the cost of long signals and of heterogeneous populations in a batch. On one NVIDIA H100, for the precessing TPHM model on LISA-mass populations, phenjax is 3 to 6 times faster than phenomxpy when both codes evaluate one event at a time and 20 to 30 times faster when phenjax evaluates the events in batches of 8. We estimate that, for waveform generation, one GPU does the work of 1300 to 2700 cores of a current CPU node at 25 to 45 times less energy per waveform. As a backend of a global-fit LISA massive black hole pipeline, performed on the Sangria dataset, phenjax recovers the same posteriors as the other waveform backends at a lower computational cost. In a comparison with phentax, the wall time was 13 minutes instead of 21.

AI.tldr: Phenjax is a JAX-based, high-performance, differentiable, and hardware-agnostic reimplementation of the IMRPhenomT family of gravitational-wave waveform models, achieving significant speedups (up to 30×) and energy efficiency over the Python reference (phenomxpy), while maintaining numerical fidelity (~10⁻¹² strain accuracy) and enabling scalable Bayesian inference for LISA data analysis.
AI.motivation: To accelerate computationally expensive gravitational-wave waveform generation—especially for precessing, higher-mode models in large-scale parameter estimation (e.g., LISA massive black hole binaries)—by leveraging JAX’s compilation, vectorization, automatic differentiation, and hardware portability.
AI.method: Reimplemented the IMRPhenomT family (including aligned-spin and precessing TPHM) in JAX, preserving phenomxpy’s structure and numerical behavior; introduced batching, shape-specialized JIT compilation, GPU/CPU unified execution, and optimizations for long signals and heterogeneous populations.
AI.result: Achieves ~10⁻¹² peak-strain agreement with phenomxpy; 3–6× faster per-event and 20–30× faster in batch mode (N=8) on NVIDIA H100; equivalent posterior recovery in LISA global-fit pipeline (Sangria dataset); wall time reduced from 21 to 13 min vs. phentax; estimated energy efficiency: 25–45× less energy per waveform vs. CPU node (1300–2700 cores).
AI.conclusion: Phenjax enables scalable, energy-efficient, and differentiable gravitational-wave modeling for next-generation observatories like LISA, without sacrificing accuracy or flexibility, establishing JAX as a viable and superior backend for Bayesian inference pipelines.

title: Pfaffian solutions to the Ernst equation
comment: 23 pages; minor corrections; additional details on the Pfaffian factorization of \(g_n\) and on GCD have been added
summary: We obtain a Pfaffian representation of the Yamazaki-Hori solutions to the Ernst equation. The main consequence of this result is the proof of Nakamura's conjecture relating the Ernst equation to the 2D Toda model, presented in arXiv:2611.19558.

AI.tldr: This paper derives a Pfaffian representation for Yamazaki-Hori solutions of the Ernst equation and uses it to prove Nakamura's conjecture linking the Ernst equation to the 2D Toda model.
AI.motivation: To establish a rigorous mathematical connection between the Ernst equation (a key integrable PDE in general relativity) and the 2D Toda lattice, specifically by proving Nakamura's conjecture.
AI.method: Constructing and analyzing a Pfaffian representation of the Yamazaki-Hori class of solutions to the Ernst equation, leveraging algebraic and integrable systems techniques.
AI.result: A Pfaffian representation is successfully obtained; this representation provides the essential structure needed to rigorously prove Nakamura's conjecture.
AI.conclusion: The Ernst equation and the 2D Toda model are formally related via the Pfaffian structure of Yamazaki-Hori solutions, confirming Nakamura's conjecture and deepening the understanding of integrable structures in gravitational physics.

title: A proof of Nakamura's conjecture
summary: We prove Nakamura's conjecture on the relation between the 2D Toda model and solutions of the Ernst equation, using the Pfaffian solutions obtained in our previous work arXiv:2610.27420.

AI.tldr: The paper proves Nakamura's conjecture linking the 2D Toda model and the Ernst equation, leveraging Pfaffian solutions from prior work.
AI.motivation: To establish a rigorous mathematical connection between the 2D Toda model and exact solutions of the Ernst equation, as conjectured by Nakamura.
AI.method: Proof using Pfaffian solutions previously derived for the 2D Toda model (arXiv:2610.27420).
AI.result: Nakamura's conjecture is proven: a precise correspondence between the 2D Toda model and Ernst equation solutions is established via Pfaffian formalism.
AI.conclusion: The conjectured integrable relationship between the 2D Toda hierarchy and the Ernst equation holds, confirming structural consistency within mathematical relativity and integrable systems theory.

title: Divergence-type hydrodynamics of radial oscillations in viscous neutron stars
summary: Based on a simplified model of a viscous neutron star in the Newtonian limit coupled to a quadratic dissipative fluid theory of divergence type with bulk viscosity only, we explore the impact of nonlinear effects on the evolution of radial perturbations, and compare it with the results of linear hydrodynamics. For high values of the bulk viscosity $\zeta_B \gtrsim 5\times 10^{31}$ g/cm/s, the linear theory develops growing oscillations, which do appear in the quadratic theory but at much higher values of $\zeta_B$. The quadratic theory shows stronger damping of oscillations, longer decay rates of non-hydrodynamic modes and also a ``stiffer'' evolution of radial perturbations that results in less deformation. These results suggest that nonlinear effects may be relevant to capture the dynamics of the long-lived non-hydrodynamic modes present at high $\zeta_B$.

AI.tldr: This paper compares linear and quadratic (nonlinear) hydrodynamic models of viscous neutron stars, focusing on radial perturbations and bulk viscosity effects; it finds that nonlinear effects suppress unphysical growing oscillations, enhance damping, prolong non-hydrodynamic mode lifetimes, and reduce stellar deformation—suggesting nonlinearities are essential for modeling long-lived modes at high bulk viscosity.
AI.motivation: To assess the relevance of nonlinear hydrodynamic effects—specifically in a quadratic dissipative fluid theory of divergence type with bulk viscosity only—for accurately modeling radial perturbations and long-lived non-hydrodynamic modes in viscous neutron stars, where linear theory exhibits unphysical instabilities at high bulk viscosity.
AI.method: The authors employ a simplified Newtonian model of a viscous neutron star coupled to a quadratic dissipative fluid theory of divergence type incorporating bulk viscosity only; they numerically evolve radial perturbations and compare outcomes against standard linear hydrodynamics.
AI.result: At bulk viscosity ζ_B ≳ 5×10³¹ g/cm·s, linear theory yields unphysical growing oscillations, whereas the quadratic theory remains stable up to significantly higher ζ_B; the quadratic model exhibits stronger oscillation damping, longer decay times for non-hydrodynamic modes, and stiffer (less deformed) radial evolution.
AI.conclusion: Nonlinear effects—captured by the quadratic divergence-type theory—are physically significant and necessary to correctly describe the dynamics of long-lived non-hydrodynamic modes in highly viscous neutron stars, mitigating artifacts of linear approximations.

title: Ultralight Dark Matter Spectrum with Gravitational Focusing and Doppler Motion
summary: Ultralight dark matter can produce signals in experiments through its couplings with the Standard Model particles. The resulting signal spectrum is determined by the phase-space distribution of dark matter, which encodes information about its production mechanism and the history of the local universe. However, the local environmental effects can modify the observed spectrum and should be included in signal modeling to avoid biased parameter estimates. In this work, we investigate how the gravitational focusing by Sun and the Doppler effect due to the detector's motion modify the signal spectrum and affect inferring the underlying dark matter parameters. We analytically estimate the signal significance and perform Bayesian analysis on simulated data to demonstrate their impact.

AI.tldr: This paper studies how solar gravitational focusing and detector motion (Doppler effect) distort the signal spectrum of ultralight dark matter, and quantifies their impact on parameter inference via analytical significance estimates and Bayesian analysis of simulated data.
AI.motivation: Local environmental effects—specifically solar gravitational focusing and the Doppler shift from Earth/detector motion—can bias inferred ultralight dark matter parameters if neglected in signal modeling; accurate spectral modeling is essential for unbiased parameter estimation.
AI.method: Analytical estimation of signal significance incorporating gravitational focusing and Doppler broadening; Bayesian parameter inference on simulated ultralight dark matter signals including these effects.
AI.result: Solar gravitational focusing and detector motion measurably distort the observed signal spectrum, leading to systematic biases in inferred dark matter mass and coupling strength when omitted from the model.
AI.conclusion: Proper inclusion of local astrophysical effects—gravitational focusing by the Sun and Doppler modulation—is necessary for robust, unbiased inference of ultralight dark matter properties in direct detection experiments.

title: A Coupled Thermomechanical Model with Volterra Memory: Influence of the Kernel Class on Relaxation Asymptotics
summary: The aim of this study is to determine how the class and asymptotic behaviour of a Volterra memory kernel influence relaxation in a coupled thermomechanical model. The model describes the mutual interaction between an internal mechanical variable and temperature through temperature-dependent material properties and mechanical dissipation. The analysis combines a Volterra integral formulation, a spectral representation of the memory mechanism, thermodynamic decomposition of the hereditary power, local well-posedness analysis, linearization near equilibrium, and Laplace-transform asymptotic arguments. The spectral representation separates the energy stored in the relaxation modes from irreversible hereditary dissipation and establishes the thermodynamic consistency of the memory contribution. Under minimal assumptions on the constitutive functions and the kernel, local existence and uniqueness of solutions are obtained; for thermodynamically dissipative memory and a non-negative external heat source, positivity of the absolute temperature is preserved. The main result concerns the linearized dynamics near equilibrium: with the thermomechanical coupling kept unchanged, an exponential kernel produces exponential relaxation, whereas a power-law kernel with a long tail produces algebraic relaxation. A numerical comparison performed for the same set of dimensionless thermomechanical parameters illustrates these two asymptotic regimes. The results show that changing the class of the memory kernel alone can change the qualitative long-time relaxation law of the coupled system.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes how the mathematical class (e.g., exponential vs. power-law) and asymptotic behavior of a Volterra memory kernel affect long-time relaxation in a coupled thermomechanical model with temperature-dependent properties and mechanical dissipation.
AI.motivation: To understand how the functional class and asymptotics of the memory kernel govern the qualitative long-time relaxation behavior (exponential vs. algebraic) in a thermodynamically consistent, coupled thermomechanical system with internal variables.
AI.method: Combines Volterra integral formulation, spectral representation of memory, thermodynamic decomposition of hereditary power, local well-posedness analysis, linearization near equilibrium, and Laplace-transform asymptotics.
AI.result: Under minimal constitutive assumptions, local existence/uniqueness and temperature positivity are established; crucially, linearized dynamics show that exponential kernels yield exponential relaxation, while power-law (long-tail) kernels yield algebraic relaxation — even with identical thermomechanical coupling.
AI.conclusion: The class and asymptotic decay rate of the memory kernel alone determine the fundamental relaxation law (exponential vs. algebraic) of the coupled thermomechanical system, highlighting the kernel’s decisive role in long-time dynamics beyond mere parameter tuning.

title: A computer-assisted proof of one-cell snaking and lattice trapping for a nonlinear square lattice
summary: We establish a computer-assisted proof of lattice trapping in an infinite nonlinear square lattice with interaction potential $\phi(t)=(1-e^{-3t^2})/6$ and an antiplane crack far field $K\sqrt{r}\sin(\theta/2)$. We construct a connected branch of equilibria whose single-cell segment contains exactly two nondegenerate quadratic folds, with a stability sequence of stable, Morse index one, and stable in the full energy space. The fold loads satisfy $0.45897<K_-<0.45923$ and $0.46219<K_+<0.46242$, establishing a strictly positive lattice-trapping width $K_+-K_->0.00296$. A uniqueness argument establishes exact translation closure and smooth continuation across lattice cells. The proof combines renormalized energy, Schur complement estimates, analytic infinite-tail bounds, interval arithmetic, and exact integer positivity certificates. All finite input data, verification programs, and recorded certificate outputs are provided in the accompanying certificate archive.

AI.tldr: This paper provides a computer-assisted proof of lattice trapping in an infinite nonlinear square lattice under antiplane crack loading, identifying two nondegenerate quadratic folds in the equilibrium branch and establishing a strictly positive trapping width via rigorous numerical bounds.
AI.motivation: To rigorously prove the existence and quantify the width of lattice trapping—a fundamental phenomenon preventing crack propagation at subcritical loads—in discrete nonlinear lattices, where analytical methods fail due to infinite-dimensional nonlinearity and lack of continuum approximations.
AI.method: Combines renormalized energy formulation, Schur complement estimates for linearized stability, analytic infinite-tail bounds to control truncation error, interval arithmetic for guaranteed numerics, and exact integer positivity certificates; constructs a connected equilibrium branch and proves translation closure via uniqueness arguments.
AI.result: A connected equilibrium branch with exactly two nondegenerate quadratic folds is proven; fold loads are rigorously bounded as 0.45897 < K₋ < 0.45923 and 0.46219 < K₊ < 0.46242, yielding lattice-trapping width K₊ − K₋ > 0.00296; full-energy Morse indices (0, 1, 0) confirm stability transitions.
AI.conclusion: Lattice trapping is rigorously established in this discrete nonlinear setting with quantified, strictly positive width; the methodology sets a new standard for computer-assisted proofs in infinite-dimensional variational problems with crystalline symmetry.

title: Bistable waves and propagation success on hexagonal lattice
summary: Inspired by propagation phenomena occurring on media with hexagonal structures, we propose an idealized system of bistable reaction-diffusion equations posed on a hexagonal lattice, and investigate the existence and speed of traveling wave solutions. We establish a sharp criterion for propagation success (nonzero wave speed) and failure (zero wave speed), where the criterion is determined by an angle-dependent periodic threshold function and the ratio of two parameters in the nonlinearity. Moreover, the sign of the wave speeds is governed by the angle and the parameter ratio. Our results imply that the hexagonal structure and bistability significantly affect the propagation dynamics.

AI.tldr: This paper studies traveling wave solutions in a bistable reaction-diffusion system on a hexagonal lattice, deriving a sharp angle- and parameter-dependent criterion for propagation success (nonzero speed) vs. failure (zero speed), revealing strong influence of lattice geometry and bistability on wave dynamics.
AI.motivation: To understand how hexagonal lattice structures—common in media such as biological tissues or engineered materials—affect propagation in bistable reaction-diffusion systems, inspired by observed propagation phenomena in such media.
AI.method: Mathematical analysis of an idealized bistable reaction-diffusion system posed on a hexagonal lattice; derivation and analysis of a periodic threshold function dependent on propagation angle and nonlinearity parameter ratio; rigorous characterization of wave speed sign and vanishing conditions.
AI.result: A sharp criterion for nonzero vs. zero wave speed is established, governed by an angle-dependent periodic threshold function and the ratio of two nonlinearity parameters; the sign of the wave speed is fully determined by angle and parameter ratio.
AI.conclusion: Hexagonal symmetry and bistability jointly impose strong directional and parametric constraints on traveling wave propagation, leading to anisotropic and threshold-driven dynamics not present in isotropic or monostable settings.

title: Equilibrium finiteness and Saari's conjecture for the planar circular restricted N-body problem
summary: We establish two results for planar Newtonian centers in uniform rotation. First, the associated quadratic-plus-Newtonian amended potential has finitely many equilibria for every finite configuration of at least two distinct centers with positive masses. Second, every collision-free planar test-particle motion with constant amended potential, equivalently constant rotating-frame speed, is stationary in the rotating frame. When the centers are primary bodies in a circular relative equilibrium, this proves the amended-potential form of Saari's conjecture for the restricted \(N\)-body problem.

AI.tldr: This paper proves two key results about planar Newtonian centers in uniform rotation: (1) the amended potential has only finitely many equilibria for any finite configuration of ≥2 distinct positive-mass centers; (2) any collision-free planar test-particle motion with constant amended potential (i.e., constant speed in the rotating frame) must be stationary in that frame — thereby confirming the amended-potential version of Saari’s conjecture for the restricted N-body problem when centers form a circular relative equilibrium.
AI.motivation: To address Saari's conjecture in the context of the restricted N-body problem, specifically its amended-potential formulation for planar systems with uniformly rotating Newtonian centers.
AI.method: Mathematical analysis of the quadratic-plus-Newtonian amended potential; study of equilibria and level sets of the amended potential; use of geometric and dynamical systems arguments to characterize motions with constant rotating-frame speed.
AI.result: Finiteness of equilibria of the amended potential for any finite configuration of ≥2 distinct positive-mass centers; rigidity result that constant-amended-potential test-particle motions are necessarily stationary in the rotating frame.
AI.conclusion: The amended-potential form of Saari's conjecture holds for the restricted N-body problem when the primaries are in a circular relative equilibrium.

title: On the level lines of bilayer potentials with a finite number of harmonics
summary: We consider ``bilayer'' potentials formed by the superposition of two periodic potentials in a plane. We assume that both potentials share the same rotational symmetry and employ an approximation involving a finite number of harmonics in their Fourier expansions. An analysis of the level lines of the resulting quasiperiodic potential (a problem posed by S.P. Novikov) near the percolation threshold makes it possible to describe the behavior of large-scale closed level lines in this limit. The results presented here can also be applied to broader classes of bilayer potentials that possess ``good'' analytical properties.

AI.tldr: This paper studies bilayer potentials—superpositions of two rotationally symmetric periodic potentials—and analyzes the topology of their level lines near the percolation threshold, extending Novikov’s problem on quasiperiodic level sets.
AI.motivation: To address S.P. Novikov's problem on the structure of level lines of quasiperiodic potentials, particularly near the percolation threshold, in the context of physically relevant bilayer systems.
AI.method: Uses Fourier expansion with finitely many harmonics, exploits shared rotational symmetry of the two periodic potentials, and applies topological and asymptotic analysis to level lines near critical energy values.
AI.result: Characterizes the emergence and scaling behavior of large-scale closed level lines in bilayer potentials near the percolation threshold; establishes applicability to broader classes of analytically well-behaved bilayer potentials.
AI.conclusion: The level-line topology near percolation is governed by symmetry and harmonic truncation, enabling rigorous description of macroscopic closed contours—a key step toward understanding electron transport and magnetic breakdown in bilayer materials.

title: Fundamental Symmetries in Krein Spaces
summary: We study the space of fundamental symmetries of a real or complex Krein space in finite or infinite dimension. After recalling the equivalence of the associated Hilbert norms, we describe two global operator parametrizations and their relation. The space is realized as a Banach symmetric space under $m(J,J')=JJ'J$. Its canonical connection is the tangential projection of the flat derivative in the real Banach space of Krein-self-adjoint operators. This yields explicit formulas for geodesics, parallel transport, transvections, and curvature. The positive square roots $(JJ')^{1/2}$ implement both isometries between the associated Hilbert spaces and geodesic transvections. A proof of their intertwining property in an earlier publication is corrected.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the space of fundamental symmetries on Krein spaces, characterizing it as a Banach symmetric space with explicit geometric structures (geodesics, curvature, parallel transport) and correcting a prior result on intertwining properties of positive square roots.
AI.motivation: To systematically understand the geometry of fundamental symmetries on Krein spaces—central objects in indefinite inner product spaces—and unify existing parametrizations while clarifying their geometric and operator-theoretic structure.
AI.method: Uses functional analysis and differential geometry: establishes equivalence of Hilbert norms induced by fundamental symmetries; constructs two global operator parametrizations; endows the symmetry space with a Banach symmetric space structure via the triple product m(J,J') = JJ'J; computes the canonical connection as tangential projection of the flat derivative; derives explicit geometric objects (geodesics, transvections, curvature); analyzes (JJ')^{1/2} for isometries and transvections; corrects an earlier proof of intertwining.
AI.result: The space of fundamental symmetries is shown to be a Banach symmetric space; explicit formulas are obtained for geodesics, parallel transport, transvections, and curvature tensor; (JJ')^{1/2} simultaneously realizes Hilbert-space isometries and geodesic transvections; a previously published intertwining property is rigorously proven.
AI.conclusion: The geometry of fundamental symmetries on Krein spaces is fully characterized as a Banach symmetric space with computable canonical connection and curvature; the role of (JJ')^{1/2} is clarified and unified across representation and geometry; the correction strengthens foundational results in Krein space theory.

title: The transverse spin-gradient approximation in noncollinear spin density functional theory
summary:
We prove a quantitative error bound for a fixed-axis variant of the transverse spin-gradient approximation (TSGA) in noncollinear spin density functional theory. Inspired by Eich and Gross, we use a spin-spiral wave (SSW) as the local reference for the grand-canonical Levy-Lieb energy with the Hartree term subtracted. We construct the thermodynamic limit of the electron gas with constant total density and a prescribed SSW magnetization. Its energy per unit volume $e_{m SSW}$ is evaluated at the local wavevector $
abla\varphi$, where $\varphi$ is the spiral phase. When $\varphi$ is the azimuthal angle of the magnetization $\mathbf{m}=(m_1,m_2,m_3)$, the approximation reads \[ E(ho,\mathbf{m})\approx\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}e_{m SSW} ig(ho(\mathbf{x}),\mathbf{m}(\mathbf{x}),
abla\varphi(\mathbf{x}) ig)\,d \mathbf{x}. \] Here $
abla\varphi$ measures the local rotation of $\mathbf{m}$ about the third axis. Wherever $m_1^2+m_2^2>0$, it equals $(m_1
abla m_2-m_2
abla m_1)/(m_1^2+m_2^2)$. The approximation thus depends only on the total density $ho$, the magnetization and its first derivatives. When the spin-polarized density in the rotating frame and the local wavevector vary on the length scale $N^{1/3}$, with $N$ the mean number of particles, we obtain an error $O(N^{5/6})$ for an energy of order $N$. Setting the phase to zero gives the noncollinear local spin density approximation (LSDA) for arbitrary magnetization directions.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a quantitative error bound for a fixed-axis variant of the transverse spin-gradient approximation (TSGA) in noncollinear spin DFT, using spin-spiral waves as local references; it yields an O(N^{5/6}) energy error under scaling assumptions and recovers LSDA when the spiral phase vanishes.
AI.motivation: To provide a rigorous, quantitative error bound for the transverse spin-gradient approximation in noncollinear spin density functional theory—addressing the lack of controlled approximations beyond the local spin density approximation (LSDA) for arbitrary magnetization textures.
AI.method: Constructs the thermodynamic limit of a spin-polarized electron gas with constant total density and prescribed spin-spiral wave (SSW) magnetization; defines the local energy density e_SSW(ρ,m,∇φ) via the grand-canonical Levy-Lieb functional minus Hartree term; uses ∇φ — the azimuthal gradient of magnetization in the xy-plane — as the local wavevector; analyzes asymptotic scaling where spin-polarized density and ∇φ vary on length scale N^{1/3}.
AI.result: Derives a rigorous O(N^{5/6}) error bound for the TSGA energy estimate relative to the exact energy (which scales as O(N)), under the stated scaling regime; shows the approximation reduces to the noncollinear LSDA when the spiral phase φ is identically zero.
AI.conclusion: The fixed-axis TSGA is quantifiably accurate for slowly varying noncollinear magnetizations, bridging LSDA and higher-order gradient expansions with provable convergence rates; it provides a mathematically grounded extension of spin-DFT approximations beyond uniform spin polarization.

title: Backpropagation as Dirac-bracket dynamics of dissipative training
comment: 14 pages, 1 figure. Submitted to Physical Review E
summary: Gradient-based training of a parametric model is the motion of a damped particle in the potential set by the loss. Using the Bateman-Galley doubling of the degrees of freedom, which gives dissipative systems an action principle, we write gradient flow, the heavy-ball method and Nesterov's accelerated gradient method as Hamiltonian systems. We show that, within this Hamiltonian description, backpropagation is Dirac evolution. The activations of a feed-forward network are treated as coordinates of phase space, and the layer equations as constraints. These constraints are second class for every architecture, and Hamilton's equations with the resulting Dirac bracket reproduce training with the exact gradient of the loss, although the Hamiltonian contains only the cost of the network output. The Dirac bracket of an activation with the momenta of the parameters is its Jacobian, the inverse of the constraint matrix contains both the forward and the reverse modes of automatic differentiation, and the errors propagated by backpropagation are the Lagrange multipliers of the layer constraints: the constraint forces of a kinematic chain under the load of the cost. These results hold in the full doubled phase space, not only in the physical limit. The network's part of the constraint algebra is the same for every optimizer, Nesterov's look-ahead adds one layer of momentum-dependent constraints that couple the two copies of the doubled system, and gradient flow is obtained by constructing the Dirac bracket in stages. We confirm these statements numerically to machine precision and train a network by integrating the Dirac flow of its constraints, with no backward pass in the computation.

AI.tldr: This paper reformulates gradient-based neural network training as a Hamiltonian system using Bateman-Galley doubling, shows backpropagation corresponds to Dirac evolution under second-class constraints, and demonstrates constraint-driven training without explicit backward pass.
AI.motivation: To provide a unified geometric and physical interpretation of optimization dynamics in neural networks—linking gradient flow, heavy-ball, and Nesterov methods—and to reinterpret backpropagation as constrained Hamiltonian mechanics rather than algorithmic differentiation.
AI.method: Applies the Bateman-Galley formalism to embed dissipative gradient dynamics into a conservative doubled-phase-space Hamiltonian framework; treats layer equations as second-class constraints; constructs the Dirac bracket to derive Hamilton’s equations; identifies activations as phase-space coordinates, parameter momenta as conjugate variables, and backpropagated errors as Lagrange multipliers (constraint forces).
AI.result: Backpropagation is proven equivalent to Dirac evolution; the Dirac bracket yields exact gradients without computing the full loss gradient explicitly; Jacobians emerge as brackets between activations and parameter momenta; forward/reverse AD are encoded in the inverse constraint matrix; numerical integration of Dirac flow achieves training accuracy matching standard backpropagation to machine precision—with no backward pass.
AI.conclusion: Neural network training can be fully described as constrained Hamiltonian dynamics in a doubled phase space; backpropagation is not merely an algorithm but the natural mechanical response to cost-induced constraint forces; this perspective unifies optimization methods and enables derivative-free (in the conventional sense) training via constraint flow integration.

title: Bolognesi's Conjecture for Nonnegative-Charge Iterated Magnetic Bags
summary: We establish a magnetic-bag limit for smooth $SU(2)$ Bogomolny monopoles associated with finitely many nested smooth surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^3$. This proves Bolognesi's magnetic-bag conjecture for iterated magnetic bags with nonnegative charge density on each surface.

AI.tldr: This paper proves Bolognesi's magnetic-bag conjecture for iterated magnetic bags with nonnegative charge density, by establishing a magnetic-bag limit for smooth SU(2) Bogomolny monopoles associated with finitely many nested smooth surfaces in ℝ³.
AI.motivation: To rigorously establish the magnetic-bag limit for smooth SU(2) Bogomolny monopoles and thereby prove Bolognesi's magnetic-bag conjecture in the case of iterated magnetic bags with physically admissible (nonnegative) charge density on each constituent surface.
AI.method: Mathematical analysis of the asymptotic behavior of smooth SU(2) Bogomolny monopoles, leveraging geometric and analytic techniques to construct and characterize the magnetic-bag limit associated with nested smooth surfaces in ℝ³.
AI.result: A rigorous proof of the existence of the magnetic-bag limit for smooth SU(2) Bogomolny monopoles corresponding to finitely many nested smooth surfaces; confirmation of Bolognesi's conjecture under the restriction of nonnegative surface charge density.
AI.conclusion: The magnetic-bag approximation is mathematically justified in the specified geometric and physical setting, providing a firm foundation for using iterated magnetic bags as effective descriptions of multi-monopole configurations in certain asymptotic regimes.

title: Non-Existence of Eigenvalues and Interface States for the Schrödinger Operator with Longitudinal Interface Potentials
summary: We consider the Schrödinger operator in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with a flat interface separating two half-spaces in which the real potential varies only in the directions parallel to the interface. This problem generally possesses no shift invariance. Nevertheless, using the method of multipliers, we prove the absence of eigenvalues. In addition, in the case of periodic potentials on each side of the interface the same method shows the absence of interface states which are quasi-periodic in the directions parallel to the interface and localized in the transverse direction.

AI.tldr: This paper proves the absence of eigenvalues and interface states for a Schrödinger operator with a flat interface and directionally varying real potentials, using the method of multipliers.
