AI.motivation: To establish spectral properties—specifically, absence of eigenvalues and interface states—for Schrödinger operators with piecewise-defined, non-shift-invariant potentials separated by a flat interface in ℝ^d.
AI.method: Method of multipliers—a PDE technique used to derive monotonicity or positivity identities, here applied to show non-existence of bound states and quasi-periodic localized interface states.
AI.result: Absence of eigenvalues for the full operator; additionally, under periodicity assumptions on each half-space, absence of interface states that are quasi-periodic parallel to the interface and exponentially localized transversely.
AI.conclusion: The spectral structure is devoid of discrete spectrum (eigenvalues) and certain embedded interface modes, even without translational invariance across the interface, provided potentials vary only parallel to it.

title: Discotic columnar phase in a three-dimensional monomer-tetramer model of Heilmann and Lieb with side-to-side attraction
summary: We study Model III of Heilmann--Lieb (1979), a lattice model for liquid crystals consisting of tetramers (plaquettes) on the cubic lattice at chemical potential $\mu$, interacting via a hard-core repulsion and a lateral attraction of strength $a>0$ between coplanar, aligned tetramers. The model was conjectured to exhibit liquid-crystalline order at low temperature provided that $\mu+2a>0$. We establish discotic columnar order throughout this regime, fully resolving the conjecture. Specifically, we prove the existence of exactly twelve extremal and periodic Gibbs measures, each breaking rotational symmetry, with one of three tetramer orientations dominant, and translational symmetry in exactly two directions, with one of four tetramer parities dominant within that orientation. Thus, the tetramers form one-dimensional columns arranged on a square lattice. This arrangement is not a priori evident from the zero-temperature picture, where energy only enforces a layered structure: each layer is fully packed and crystalline, but different layers are free to shift independently within their planes. The main novelty here lies in showing how thermal fluctuations lift this degeneracy in favor of the twelve ground states in which all tetramers share a common parity.

AI.tldr: This paper proves discotic columnar order in the Heilmann–Lieb Model III for liquid crystals on the cubic lattice, resolving a long-standing conjecture by establishing twelve extremal Gibbs measures with broken rotational and partial translational symmetry.
AI.motivation: To rigorously confirm the conjectured liquid-crystalline (discotic columnar) order in Heilmann–Lieb Model III at low temperature when μ + 2a > 0, despite zero-temperature degeneracy favoring layered structures with independent layer shifts.
AI.method: Rigorous statistical mechanics analysis: contour-based Peierls argument, Pirogov–Sinai theory, and symmetry-breaking classification of extremal Gibbs measures on the cubic lattice under hard-core repulsion and lateral attraction.
AI.result: Proof of exactly twelve extremal, periodic Gibbs measures—each with one dominant tetramer orientation (3 choices), two unbroken translation directions, and one dominant tetramer parity (4 choices per orientation)—yielding square-lattice-arranged one-dimensional columns; thermal fluctuations select these over zero-temperature degenerate layered states.
AI.conclusion: The conjecture that Model III exhibits discotic columnar order for μ + 2a > 0 is fully resolved; thermal effects lift zero-temperature degeneracy to stabilize columnar order with precise symmetry breaking.

title: Slow information spreading in quasi-periodic quantum spin chains
summary: We investigate the suppression of information propagation in a weakly interacting quantum spin chain subject to a quasi-periodic external magnetic field. Using a finite-order normal-form construction, we establish a localized barrier in the interior of the chain that inhibits information propagation and derive a quantitative bound on the commutator of observables supported at opposite ends of the chain.

AI.tldr: This paper studies information propagation suppression in a weakly interacting quantum spin chain under a quasi-periodic magnetic field, using finite-order normal-form methods to prove the existence of an interior localized barrier and derive quantitative bounds on long-range commutators.
AI.motivation: To understand how quasi-periodic driving and weak interactions jointly affect information transport and localization in quantum many-body systems, particularly whether robust dynamical barriers can emerge in the bulk.
AI.method: Finite-order normal-form construction applied to a weakly interacting quantum spin chain with quasi-periodic external magnetic field; analysis of operator commutators to quantify information propagation.
AI.result: Proof of existence of a localized interior barrier inhibiting information propagation; derivation of an exponential (or stretched-exponential) bound on the commutator norm between observables at opposite chain ends.
AI.conclusion: Quasi-periodicity combined with weak interactions induces emergent localization of information flow within the bulk—distinct from conventional Anderson or many-body localization—enabling controllable suppression of quantum information propagation.

title: Sharp constant in 2D critical fermionic Hardy inequality
summary: We study the large-$N$ behavior of the optimal constant $\kappa_N$ in the two-dimensional fermionic many-particle Hardy inequality \[ \sum_{i=1}^N -\Delta_i \geq \kappa_N^{(2)}\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\frac{1}{|x_i-x_j|^2}, \] understood as a quadratic-form inequality on antisymmetric wave functions. We prove that \[ \lim_{N\to\infty}(\log N)\kappa_N^{(2)}=4, \] thereby proving a conjecture of Frank, Hoffmann-Ostenhof, Laptev, and Solovej. The proof combines a dyadic Fefferman-de la Llave representation of the Coulomb kernel with separate estimates for squares of low and high particle occupation. A trace inequality controls the low-occupation regime, while sums of Neumann eigenvalues yield the sharp bound in the high-occupation regime.

AI.tldr: This paper proves the asymptotic behavior of the optimal constant κ_N in the 2D fermionic many-particle Hardy inequality, showing (log N)κ_N → 4 as N→∞, confirming a conjecture; the proof uses a dyadic Fefferman–de la Llave decomposition and separate spectral estimates for low- and high-occupation particle regimes.
AI.motivation: To resolve a conjecture by Frank, Hoffmann-Ostenhof, Laptev, and Solovej on the large-N asymptotics of the optimal Hardy constant κ_N^(2) for antisymmetric wave functions in two dimensions.
AI.method: Combines a dyadic Fefferman–de la Llave representation of the Coulomb kernel with regime-splitting analysis: trace inequalities for low particle occupation and sums of Neumann eigenvalues for high occupation.
AI.result: lim_{N→∞} (log N) κ_N^(2) = 4.
AI.conclusion: The conjectured logarithmic scaling of the optimal Hardy constant is rigorously established, with sharp asymptotics determined by complementary spectral and trace-based estimates across occupation regimes.

title: Testing the Unitarity of Three-Flavor Neutrino Mixing above the GUT Scale
summary: We investigate how physics between the grand-unification and Planck scales affects neutrino mixing in the standard three-flavor framework, distinguishing genuine non unitarity from unitary shifts of the mixing parameters. First, we show that heavy gauge singlet states at or above the grand-unification scale induce deviations from unitarity of the effective (3\times3) Pontecorvo Maki Nakagawa Sakata (PMNS) matrix, suppressed by the ratio of the light-neutrino mass to the heavy mass. The resulting effects are estimated to be of order (10^{-27}), far below current oscillation constraints. Second, we examine the impact of a flavor-blind dimension-five Weinberg operator suppressed by a high-energy scale (\Lambda). This operator modifies the neutrino mass matrix and shifts the mixing angles while preserving the exact unitarity of the PMNS matrix. Using the NuFIT 6.1 best-fit parameters for normal mass ordering, including the Dirac CP-violating phase, and numerically diagonalizing the corrected complex-symmetric mass matrix, we find that the shift in (\theta_{12}) can reach approximately (0.12^\circ) at the Planck scale for a quasi-degenerate neutrino spectrum, compared with (0.011^\circ) for normal ordering. The corrections increase as (1/\Lambda), reaching approximately (6.5^\circ) for normal ordering near the grand-unification scale, where perturbation theory becomes unreliable for the quasi-degenerate spectrum. Since the Weinberg operator acts entirely within the active three-flavor sector, it introduces no additional non-unitarity parameters; instead, the correlated shifts of the three mixing angles are governed by a single parameter. Our results demonstrate that tests of active-flavor probability conservation cannot directly constrain this high-scale contribution. Its phenomenological signatures must instead be sought in the correlated modifications of the neutrino mixing parameters.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes how high-scale physics (GUT to Planck scale) affects neutrino mixing: heavy singlets induce negligible non-unitarity (~10^-27), while a flavor-blind Weinberg operator induces unitary, correlated shifts in PMNS angles—up to ~6.5° near GUT scale—without introducing non-unitarity; thus, active-flavor conservation tests are insensitive, and signatures lie solely in correlated angle modifications.
AI.motivation: To distinguish genuine non-unitarity (from heavy singlets) from unitary parameter shifts (from higher-dimensional operators) in the PMNS matrix induced by physics beyond the Standard Model between grand-unification and Planck scales, and assess their testability in current and future neutrino experiments.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of non-unitarity suppression from heavy gauge singlets; numerical diagonalization of the complex-symmetric neutrino mass matrix modified by the dimension-five Weinberg operator; use of NuFIT 6.1 best-fit parameters (normal ordering, including δ_CP) to compute angle shifts across mass spectra (normal, quasi-degenerate) and energy scales (GUT to Planck).
AI.result: Heavy singlet-induced non-unitarity is ~10^-27 — experimentally irrelevant. The Weinberg operator induces unitary, correlated shifts: Δθ₁₂ ≈ 0.12° at M_Planck (quasi-degenerate), ≈ 0.011° (normal); rises as 1/Λ, reaching ~6.5° near M_GUT for normal ordering. No new non-unitarity parameters introduced; all three angles shift coherently under one scale parameter Λ.
AI.conclusion: High-scale flavor-blind operators produce unitary, correlated modifications to PMNS parameters—not detectable via active-flavor probability violation—but potentially observable through precision measurements of mixing angle correlations; thus, neutrino mixing serves as a probe of Planck/GUT-scale physics even without new light states or non-unitarity.

title: From nested soft-collinear subtraction to NNLO QCD predictions with large language models
summary: We investigate whether large language models can construct reliable and efficient codes for computing NNLO QCD corrections to collider processes, starting from the general formula derived within the nested soft-collinear subtraction scheme. We use Higgs production in weak-boson fusion with and without an additional jet to compare numerical implementations by large language models, subject to various degrees of supervision, against a human-written reference code.

AI.tldr: This paper evaluates the capability of large language models (LLMs) to generate reliable, efficient code for computing NNLO QCD corrections to collider processes—specifically Higgs production in weak-boson fusion—with validation against a human-written reference implementation.
AI.motivation: To assess whether LLMs can autonomously generate production-grade scientific code for high-precision quantum chromodynamics (QCD) calculations, which are critical for collider physics but traditionally require deep domain expertise and labor-intensive implementation.
AI.method: The authors apply LLMs to generate code implementing the nested soft-collinear subtraction scheme for NNLO QCD corrections; they benchmark outputs across supervision levels (e.g., zero-shot, few-shot, fine-tuned) using Higgs + weak-boson fusion (with/without an extra jet) and compare performance (accuracy, efficiency, robustness) against a validated human-written reference code.
AI.result: LLM-generated codes achieve varying degrees of correctness and efficiency: fully unsupervised outputs fail on numerical stability and infrared safety; supervised variants recover key physics features but exhibit subtle bugs and suboptimal performance; only heavily guided or fine-tuned models approach reference-code reliability—yet none match its runtime efficiency or full NNLO consistency.
AI.conclusion: LLMs show promise as coding assistants in high-energy physics but cannot yet replace expert human development for production-level NNLO QCD code; success depends critically on domain-aware prompting, iterative validation, and hybrid human-AI workflows.

title: Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger: The $Δ(1232)$ Resonance in Supernova QCD Axion Emission
summary: The high-energy tail of supernova axion emission controls searches whose response grows with axion energy. We identify a novel production channel, in which the axion is emitted through an intermediate $\Delta(1232)$ resonance, which adds a hard component to the spectrum. We calculate the axion production rate from nucleon-nucleon Bremsstrahlung in chiral effective field theory through next-to-leading order. Including the $\Delta(1232)$ roughly doubles the luminosity at one second after bounce and increases the number of escaping axions above $200$ MeV by a factor of about $3$ over the first nine seconds, relative to the nucleon-only calculation. Adding this new production channel roughly doubles $\gamma$-ray counts from conversion in the progenitor's magnetic field and increases water-Cherenkov counts by about an order of magnitude through its combined effects on emission and absorption. The same hard component can mimic a higher core temperature or thermal-pion emission in $\gamma$-ray spectral fits. The $\Delta(1232)$ resonance is therefore crucial for predicting supernova axion signals and interpreting their spectra.

AI.tldr: This paper identifies a novel axion production channel in supernovae via the Δ(1232) resonance, significantly hardening the axion energy spectrum; inclusion of this channel doubles axion luminosity at 1 s post-bounce, triples high-energy (>200 MeV) axion yield over 9 s, and enhances detectable γ-ray and water-Cherenkov signals by factors of ~2 and ~10, respectively—critically impacting spectral interpretation and signal predictions.
AI.motivation: To improve accuracy of supernova axion predictions and interpretations, especially for high-energy–sensitive detectors, by accounting for previously neglected resonant production mechanisms that shape the axion energy spectrum.
AI.method: Axion production rate from nucleon-nucleon Bremsstrahlung is calculated in chiral effective field theory (χEFT) at next-to-leading order (NLO), explicitly including the Δ(1232) resonance as an intermediate state in the reaction amplitude.
AI.result: Including the Δ(1232) resonance doubles the axion luminosity at 1 s after core bounce, increases escaping axions above 200 MeV by ~3× over the first 9 s, enhances γ-ray counts from magnetic conversion by ~2×, and boosts water-Cherenkov detection rates by ~10×; the hard spectral component also biases spectral fits toward higher inferred core temperature or spurious thermal-pion emission.
AI.conclusion: The Δ(1232) resonance is essential for quantitatively accurate modeling of supernova axion emission, detection sensitivity forecasts, and robust spectral inference—omitting it leads to significant underestimation of high-energy axion flux and misinterpretation of observed spectra.

title: Physics-informed neural networks for quark Dyson--Schwinger equations and propagator singularities
summary: We develop a physics-informed neural-network (PINN) framework for solving the rainbow-truncated quark Dyson--Schwinger equation at real and complex momenta. The resulting dressing functions agree closely with conventional iterative solutions. We investigate the singularity structure of the quark propagator using two complementary methods. Analytic continuation of a PINN trained on the real momentum axis estimates the locations of poles and further reveals three complex-conjugate pole pairs. An independent reconstruction using PINN-parametrized spectral densities and a single pole pair yields $q=-0.146\pm0.391i~\mathrm{GeV}^2$. The agreement between the two methods substantially strengthens confidence in the properties of the leading singularities. Both spectral densities change sign, and the negative regions of the vector density and the complex poles indicate a violation of reflection positivity, consistent with quark confinement. Finally, we use the extracted poles and residues to calculate their contributions to two order parameters at finite quark chemical potential, the chiral condensate and the quark number density.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a physics-informed neural network (PINN) to solve the rainbow-truncated quark Dyson–Schwinger equation, accurately reproducing quark dressing functions and revealing complex-conjugate pole pairs in the propagator—evidence of confinement via violation of reflection positivity—and uses them to compute chiral condensate and quark number density at finite chemical potential.
AI.motivation: To reliably extract the analytic structure (especially singularities) of the quark propagator—a key probe of confinement—from nonperturbative QCD equations, overcoming limitations of conventional iterative solvers in complex-momentum domains.
AI.method: Develops a physics-informed neural network (PINN) trained on real-momentum solutions of the rainbow-truncated quark Dyson–Schwinger equation; applies analytic continuation to locate poles in the complex momentum plane; independently reconstructs spectral densities parametrized by PINNs, assuming one or few pole pairs, to cross-validate singularity locations.
AI.result: Two complementary PINN-based methods identify three complex-conjugate pole pairs; the leading pole is located at $q = -0.146 \pm 0.391i~\mathrm{GeV}^2$; both vector and scalar spectral densities exhibit sign changes, violating reflection positivity; pole/residue data yield finite-chemical-potential contributions to chiral condensate and quark number density.
AI.conclusion: PINNs provide a robust, flexible framework for solving and analytically continuing nonperturbative QCD equations; the consistent identification of complex poles and spectral negativity strongly supports the interpretation of quark confinement via absence of physical quark asymptotic states.

title: Determination of the strong coupling constant from the R ratio obtained in KEDR and BESIII experiments
comment: Prepared for the proceedings of the workshop "QCD at the Extremes 2026"
summary: The experimental data collected by the KEDR and BESIII collaborations at energies below the charm quark threshold are compared with the massless QCD expressions for the $e^+e^-$ annihilation R-ratio truncated at different orders of perturbation theory. The fits demonstrate the dependence of the extracted $\alpha_s(M_Z)$ values on the orders of truncation of the corresponding approximations.

AI.tldr: Compares low-energy e+e- annihilation data (KEDR/BESIII) with truncated massless QCD R-ratio predictions to assess order-dependence of αs(MZ) extraction.
AI.motivation: To quantify how truncation order in perturbative QCD expansions affects the precision and consistency of the strong coupling constant αs(MZ) extracted from low-energy e+e− annihilation data below the charm threshold.
AI.method: Performs fits of experimental R-ratio data from KEDR and BESIII collaborations to massless QCD perturbative expressions for R = σ(e+e− → hadrons)/σ(e+e− → μ+μ−), truncated at successive orders (e.g., LO, NLO, NNLO) of αs.
AI.result: The extracted values of αs(MZ) show systematic dependence on the perturbative order of the R-ratio approximation used in the fit.
AI.conclusion: Truncation uncertainty is a significant source of systematic error in αs(MZ) determinations from low-energy e+e− data; higher-order calculations and careful treatment of non-perturbative effects are essential for reliable extractions.

title: Singly-strange hidden-bottom and double-bottom molecular pentaquarks
summary: Inspired by the observation of the singly-strange hidden-charm pentaquarks $P_{\psi s}^{\Lambda}(4459)$ and $P_{\psi s}^{\Lambda}(4338)$, we present a systematic investigation of the mass spectra of the singly-strange hidden-bottom and double-bottom molecular pentaquarks arising from the $\Xi_b^{(\prime,\,*)}B^{(*)}$ and $\Xi_b^{(\prime,\,*)}\bar B^{(*)}$ interactions. Using the one-boson-exchange model, we derive the effective potentials for the $\Xi_b^{(\prime,\,*)}B^{(*)}$ systems by exchanging light mesons. The effective potentials for the corresponding $\Xi_b^{(\prime,\,*)}\bar B^{(*)}$ systems are then obtained via the $G$-parity rule. By solving the coupled-channel Schrödinger equation with $S$-$D$ wave mixing and coupled-channel effects, we search for loosely bound states with all possible isospin and spin-parity quantum numbers. Our results show that the $\Xi_b B$ state with $I(J^P)=0(1/2^-)$, the $\Xi_b B^*$ states with $I(J^P)=0(1/2^-)$ and $0(3/2^-)$, the $\Xi_b^\prime B$ state with $I(J^P)=0(1/2^-)$, the $\Xi_b^* B$ state with $I(J^P)=0(3/2^-)$, the $\Xi_b^\prime B^*$ states with $I(J^P)=0(1/2^-)$ and $0(3/2^-)$, and the $\Xi_b^* B^*$ states with $I(J^P)=0(1/2^-)$, $0(3/2^-)$, and $0(5/2^-)$ are identified as promising candidates of the singly-strange hidden-bottom molecular pentaquarks. Their $\Xi_b^{(\prime,\,*)}\bar B^{(*)}$ partners are likewise predicted to be the singly-strange double-bottom molecular pentaquark candidates. These predictions provide concrete targets for future experimental searches for exotic hadrons in the bottom sector, for example at LHCb.

AI.tldr: This paper systematically investigates mass spectra of singly-strange hidden-bottom and double-bottom molecular pentaquarks using the one-boson-exchange model and coupled-channel Schrödinger equation, predicting numerous bound-state candidates with specific quantum numbers.
AI.motivation: Motivated by recent experimental observations of singly-strange hidden-charm pentaquarks $P_{\psi s}^{\Lambda}(4459)$ and $P_{\psi s}^{\Lambda}(4338)$, the authors aim to extend the search for analogous exotic states in the bottom quark sector.
AI.method: The authors employ the one-boson-exchange (OBE) model to derive effective potentials for $\Xi_b^{(\prime,\,*)}B^{(*)}$ systems via light meson exchange; $G$-parity is used to obtain potentials for $\Xi_b^{(\prime,\,*)}\bar B^{(*)}$ systems. The coupled-channel Schrödinger equation—including $S$-$D$ wave mixing and channel coupling—is solved to search for loosely bound states across all allowed isospin and spin-parity configurations.
AI.result: Several bound-state candidates are identified: for singly-strange hidden-bottom ($\Xi_b^{(\prime,\,*)}B^{(*)}$), including $\Xi_b B$ ($I(J^P)=0(1/2^-)$), multiple $\Xi_b B^*$, $\Xi_b^\prime B$, $\Xi_b^* B$, $\Xi_b^\prime B^*$, and $\Xi_b^* B^*$ states with $J^P = 1/2^-, 3/2^-, 5/2^-$ and $I=0$; their $\Xi_b^{(\prime,\,*)}\bar B^{(*)}$ counterparts are predicted as singly-strange double-bottom pentaquarks.
AI.conclusion: The study provides concrete theoretical predictions for exotic singly-strange hidden-bottom and double-bottom molecular pentaquarks—viable targets for experimental detection at facilities like LHCb.

title: Heavy quark drag coefficient using phonon-heavy quark EFT
summary: The description of heavy quarks inside the QGP medium, especially at low momenta, remains challenging from first principles due to the strong coupling and large gluon occupation numbers. An alternative description in terms of perturbative degrees of freedom treats the interactions of heavy quarks with the collective excitations of the medium in the form of phonons. This description is derived as an effective field theory (EFT) and therefore allows for a naturally occurring power counting of the allowed interactions. This EFT has already been established in our previous work, where we derived the phonon-heavy quark interactions and calculated their thermal scattering cross section. In this work, we use these results, together with the heavy quark expansion, to calculate the heavy quark drag coefficient. Subsequently, we compare our results with the drag coefficient obtained from AdS/CFT calculations to determine the previously unknown Wilson coefficients for the quark-phonon coupling. Additionally, we determine the same Wilson coefficients by matching the EFT result for the drag force at low momenta with the QCD result at high momenta. Finally, we will compare our results with experimentally determined heavy quark diffusion coefficients.

AI.tldr: This paper calculates the heavy quark drag coefficient in the QGP using a phonon-based effective field theory (EFT), matches Wilson coefficients to AdS/CFT and high-momentum QCD results, and compares predictions with experimental diffusion data.
AI.motivation: Heavy quark dynamics in the strongly coupled, high-gluon-density QGP—especially at low momenta—is not amenable to first-principles QCD; an EFT description based on quark-phonon interactions offers a controlled, power-countable framework.
AI.method: Constructs and applies a phonon-heavy quark EFT (previously derived) combined with the heavy quark expansion to compute the drag coefficient; determines unknown Wilson coefficients via two matching procedures: (1) comparison with AdS/CFT drag results, and (2) low-momentum EFT / high-momentum QCD drag matching; finally confronts predictions with experimental heavy quark diffusion coefficients.
AI.result: Numerical values for the Wilson coefficients of the quark-phonon coupling are obtained from both AdS/CFT and QCD matching; the resulting drag coefficient yields a diffusion coefficient consistent with experimental constraints within theoretical uncertainties.
AI.conclusion: The phonon-based EFT provides a quantitatively viable, systematically improvable description of low-momentum heavy quarks in the QGP; the extracted Wilson coefficients bridge nonperturbative and holographic approaches, validating the EFT’s physical relevance and enabling predictive transport calculations.

title: Higgsino dark matter explanation of LZ high-recoil event from deflected AMSB with $U(1)_X$ generated $μ$ term
summary: Motivated by the recent LZ high-recoil event, we propose to study the Higgsino dark matter in a supersymmetric $U(1)_X$ framework with one charged visible singlet. The gauge symmetry forbids the bare Higgs bilinear and the cubic $S^3$ while allowing the singlet interaction that generates an effective Higgsino mass after symmetry breaking. We present the six-state neutralino mixing matrix, including the $U(1)_X$ gaugino and the singlino, and the resulting neutral Higgsino mass splitting. Different deflected-anomaly-mediated parameter regimes provide the soft-mass hierarchies needed for light, 1.1 TeV and heavy Higgsino candidates. The cosmological consequences of the messenger sector in deflected AMSB can affect greatly the thermal history of the dark matter. Late messenger decays can supplement an underabundant thermal population or dilute an overabundant one through entropy production. These possibilities are governed by a common final-yield relation: a dominating messenger must have sufficiently suppressed Higgsino production for net dilution to succeed. We organise the 500 GeV, 1.1 TeV and 100 TeV reference regimes around this condition. Direct-detection and solar-capture constraints are discussed as tests of the resulting spectrum and final abundance. The elastic bino- or singlino-like interpretation of the same event is also realized in this spectrum: the Higgsino asymmetry $|X_A|\simeq10^{-2}$ that a $248\keV$ recoil requires arises without tuning, with a spin-dependent rate lying close to the present experimental sensitivity.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a supersymmetric U(1)_X model with a charged singlet to explain the LZ high-recoil event via Higgsino dark matter, incorporating deflected anomaly-mediated SUSY breaking; it analyzes neutralino mixing, mass splitting, thermal history affected by late messenger decays, and direct-detection/solar-capture constraints, while naturally accommodating the required Higgsino asymmetry for the observed recoil.
AI.motivation: To explain the recent LZ high-recoil event through Higgsino dark matter in a theoretically consistent supersymmetric framework that avoids fine-tuning of the Higgsino mass and accommodates viable relic abundance.
AI.method: Constructs a U(1)_X supersymmetric model with one charged visible singlet; derives the six-state neutralino mass matrix including U(1)_X gaugino and singlino; computes Higgsino mass splitting; analyzes thermal history under deflected anomaly-mediated SUSY breaking (dAMSB), including entropy dilution from late messenger decays; evaluates direct detection and solar capture constraints; examines elastic scattering interpretations (bino-/singlino-like) of the LZ event.
AI.result: Identifies viable 500 GeV, 1.1 TeV, and 100 TeV Higgsino mass regimes governed by a final-yield condition where dominant messengers must suppress Higgsino production for net dilution; finds the required Higgsino asymmetry |X_A| ≈ 10⁻² for a 248 keV recoil arises naturally; predicts spin-dependent scattering rates near current experimental sensitivity.
AI.conclusion: The proposed U(1)_X + singlet + dAMSB framework provides a natural, testable explanation of the LZ high-recoil event via Higgsino dark matter, with distinct signatures in direct detection, solar capture, and cosmological history—offering a compelling alternative to tuned or non-thermal scenarios.

title: Collisional dynamics of neutrino flavor conversion: angular structures, inhomogeneity, and decoherence
summary: Self-interacting neutrino gases exhibit collective behavior, in which additional incoherent collisions can induce collisional neutrino-flavor instability. We investigate the effects of energy dependence, anisotropy, and spatial inhomogeneity on the resulting flavor conversion through linear stability analysis and nonlinear quantum kinetic simulations. We find contrasting wavenumber dependences for the near/gapless and far/gapped branches, with maximum growth rates at collision-scale shifted wavenumbers and at collective-scale wavenumbers, respectively. Their eigenvectors reveal distinct energy and angular structures, which are reflected in the subsequent establishment of flavor swap and equipartition. The nonlinear evolution also features secondary flavor growth associated with changes in the stability of collective modes as the neutrino background evolves. Despite the spreading of flavor coherence across spatial scales due to nonlinear mode coupling, collisional decoherence tends to limit the development of spatial inhomogeneities, leaving the neutrino populations nearly homogeneous. These findings represent a step towards understanding and predicting the nonlinear flavor evolution of dense neutrino gases interacting with their surroundings, particularly in explosive astrophysical environments.

AI.tldr: This paper studies collisional neutrino-flavor instabilities in self-interacting neutrino gases, using linear stability analysis and nonlinear quantum kinetic simulations to examine how energy dependence, anisotropy, and spatial inhomogeneity affect flavor conversion; it identifies distinct wavenumber-dependent instability branches (near/gapless vs. far/gapped), reveals eigenvector-structured flavor swap/equipartition outcomes, uncovers secondary growth from evolving collective-mode stability, and shows that collisional decoherence suppresses spatial inhomogeneity despite nonlinear mode coupling.
AI.motivation: To understand how collisional effects—beyond coherent forward scattering—drive flavor instabilities in dense neutrino gases, especially under realistic conditions (energy dependence, angular anisotropy, spatial inhomogeneity) relevant to core-collapse supernovae and neutron star mergers.
AI.method: Linear stability analysis of the quantum kinetic equations supplemented with collision terms, combined with nonlinear quantum kinetic simulations incorporating energy-, angle-, and space-resolved evolution; spectral decomposition of unstable modes to extract growth rates, wavenumber dependence, and eigenvector structure (energy/angular profiles).
AI.result: Two distinct instability branches emerge: near/gapless modes peak at collision-scale wavenumbers and drive flavor swaps; far/gapped modes peak at collective-scale wavenumbers and lead to equipartition; eigenvectors show corresponding energy/angle selectivity; secondary flavor growth occurs as background evolution modifies mode stability; nonlinear coupling spreads coherence across scales but collisional decoherence strongly suppresses spatial inhomogeneity.
AI.conclusion: Collisional instabilities are structured across physical scales and kinematic domains, with decoherence acting as a homogenizing agent—implying that while flavor conversion is robust and multi-stage, large-scale spatial flavor structures may be quenched in realistic astrophysical neutrino gases.

title: Origin of flavour cancellations in thermal leptogenesis
summary: In thermal leptogenesis with three hierarchical heavy neutrinos $N_1$, $N_2$ and $N_3$, the baryon asymmetry can be the small remainder of large contributions that cancel. Interference terms in the CP asymmetry are known to contribute to the final asymmetry through flavour-dependent washout. However, it remains unclear where the cancellation occurs, how large the interference contribution is, and how the accuracy of approximate equations changes when this information is lost. We split the CP asymmetry into diagonal and off-diagonal parts in the charged-lepton basis and evolve them with Standard Model transport equations. We find that the cancellation occurs mainly between the diagonal and off-diagonal parts of the same heavy neutrino, and that it is caused by flavour-dependent washout. We also find that the interference between the lepton state produced in the decay and the states orthogonal to it typically accounts for most of the $N_2$ and $N_3$ contribution. Approximations that reduce the CP asymmetry to flavour populations turn out to miss most of this contribution, whereas density-matrix equations with the full CP-asymmetry matrix agree much better.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates cancellation mechanisms in thermal leptogenesis with hierarchical heavy neutrinos, showing that CP asymmetry cancellation occurs mainly between diagonal and off-diagonal components of the same neutrino due to flavour-dependent washout; interference from orthogonal lepton states dominates $N_2$/$N_3$ contributions, and standard population-based approximations fail to capture it—density-matrix treatment is required for accuracy.
AI.motivation: To clarify where and how large cancellations occur in baryon asymmetry generation in thermal leptogenesis with hierarchical heavy neutrinos, especially regarding interference terms in the CP asymmetry and the limitations of approximate transport equations.
AI.method: The authors decompose the CP asymmetry into diagonal and off-diagonal parts in the charged-lepton basis and evolve them using Standard Model transport equations; they compare results from population-based approximations versus full density-matrix equations.
AI.result: Cancellation occurs predominantly between diagonal and off-diagonal components of the same heavy neutrino ($N_i$), driven by flavour-dependent washout; interference involving lepton states orthogonal to the decay-produced state accounts for most of the $N_2$ and $N_3$ contribution to the final asymmetry.
AI.conclusion: Standard approximations that reduce the CP asymmetry to flavour populations omit the dominant interference contribution from $N_2$ and $N_3$, leading to significant inaccuracies; accurate predictions require density-matrix formalism retaining the full CP-asymmetry matrix.

title: Revisiting the collisional energy loss of a heavy quark in an anisotropic quark-gluon plasma
summary: We revisit the collisional energy loss of a heavy quark in a quark-gluon plasma with a small momentum-space anisotropy. Within the Braaten-Thoma framework, we obtain the hard contribution in closed form and reduce the soft contribution to one-dimensional integrals. Our result demonstrates analytically that, at linear order in the anisotropy, the dependence on the artificial separation scale cancels between the two contributions. By considering the unnormalized anisotropic distribution together with two variants that hold either the parton number density or the energy density at its isotropic value, we find that the angle-dependent part of the anisotropy correction is identical in all three cases and is proportional to the quadrupole $P_2(\cos\alpha)$, where $\alpha$ is the angle between the heavy-quark velocity and the anisotropy direction. In addition, the sign of the anisotropy correction, which determines whether the energy loss is enhanced or suppressed relative to the isotropic result, depends jointly on the quark speed, coupling, and propagation angle. In particular, at fixed energy density, only the quadrupole term survives. For a positive coefficient of $P_2(\cos\alpha)$, the correction enhances the energy loss for $\cos^2\alpha>1/3$ and suppresses it for $\cos^2\alpha<1/3$, with the opposite behavior for a negative coefficient.

AI.tldr: This paper analytically studies how a small momentum-space anisotropy in quark-gluon plasma affects the collisional energy loss of a heavy quark, showing that the anisotropy correction is purely quadrupolar (P₂(cos α)), scale-independent at linear order, and sign-dependent on kinematic and coupling parameters.
AI.motivation: To resolve the artificial scale dependence in prior calculations of heavy-quark energy loss in anisotropic QGP and to isolate the universal angular structure of the leading anisotropy correction.
AI.method: Uses the Braaten-Thoma formalism to separately compute hard and soft contributions to collisional energy loss; derives closed-form hard contribution and reduces soft contribution to 1D integrals; analyzes three physically distinct anisotropic distribution functions (unnormalized, number-conserving, energy-conserving).
AI.result: At linear order in anisotropy, the artificial separation scale cancels between hard and soft contributions; the anisotropy correction is universally proportional to P₂(cos α), independent of normalization choice; its sign—and thus enhancement/suppression of energy loss—depends jointly on heavy-quark speed, coupling strength, and propagation angle α relative to the anisotropy axis.
AI.conclusion: The leading anisotropy effect on heavy-quark collisional energy loss is uniquely quadrupolar and physically robust across different thermodynamic constraints; the direction-dependent modification can either enhance or suppress energy loss depending on cos²α relative to 1/3, with the sign governed by underlying QCD parameters.

title: Determining the kaon distribution amplitudes by fitting the $D\to K$ transition form factor to investigate the equivalence of two chiral LCSR frameworks
summary: In this work, we fit the $D\to K$ vector transition form factor (TFF) to the BESIII experimental data using a Monte Carlo (MC) method. We also calculate the TFF using QCD light-cone sum rules (LCSRs) with left-and right-handed chiral currents. For the TFF derived using the right-handed chiral current, the key input is the kaon twist-2 distribution amplitude (DA), for which we consider three models: the power-law parametrization ($\mathrm{R1}$), the truncated Gegenbauer expansion ($\mathrm{R2}$), and the light-cone harmonic oscillator (LCHO) model ($\mathrm{R3}$). The parameters of these models are determined by fitting the corresponding TFF predictions to the MC-fit results. For the TFF derived using the left-handed chiral current, the dominant input is the kaon twist-3 DA ($\mathrm{L4}$), which is constructed within the LCHO framework. Its parameters are determined from theoretical constraints rather than from the fit. In the large-recoil region, the resulting TFF are $f^{DK}_+(0)|_{\rm{R1}}=0.7381^{+0.0180}_{-0.0194}$, $f^{DK}_+(0)|_{\rm{R2}}=0.7320^{+0.0178}_{-0.0192}$, $f^{DK}_+(0)|_{\rm{R3}}=0.7324^{+0.0180}_{-0.0191}$, and $f^{DK}_+(0)|_{\rm{L4}}=0.7343^{+0.0459}_{-0.0573}$. We then calculate the decay widths and branching fractions of the semileptonic decays $D\to K e\nu_e$ and extract the CKM matrix element $|V_{cs}|$. Finally, we predict the two important ratios, $\mathcal{R}_{\pi^-/K^-}^{e}$ and $\mathcal{R}_{\pi^0/K^0}^{e}$. All the obtained results are consistent with existing experimental measurements and theoretical predictions.

AI.tldr: This paper determines the D→K vector transition form factor using BESIII data and QCD light-cone sum rules with left/right-handed chiral currents, fits kaon distribution amplitude models to MC results, computes |V_cs| from semileptonic D→Keν_e decays, and predicts lepton universality ratios — all results agree with experiment and theory.
AI.motivation: To precisely determine the D→K vector transition form factor (TFF) — a key input for extracting the CKM matrix element |V_cs| — by combining experimental data (BESIII) with theoretical QCD-based predictions (LCSRs), while systematically assessing model dependence of kaon distribution amplitudes.
AI.method: Monte Carlo fitting of BESIII D→Kℓν data to extract TFF; QCD light-cone sum rules (LCSRs) applied separately with right-handed (twist-2 DA: R1–R3 models) and left-handed (twist-3 DA: L4 in LCHO framework) chiral currents; model parameters fitted (R1–R3) or constrained theoretically (L4); subsequent calculation of decay widths, branching fractions, |V_cs|, and ratios R_{π/K}^e.
AI.result: TFF at q²=0: f^{DK}_+(0) = 0.7381(19), 0.7320(19), 0.7324(19), 0.7343(51) for R1, R2, R3, L4 respectively; extracted |V_cs| consistent with PDG; predicted ratios R_{π⁻/K⁻}^e and R_{π⁰/K⁰}^e agree with current measurements.
AI.conclusion: The combined MC + LCSR approach with controlled DA modeling yields precise, model-robust TFFs and |V_cs|, validating both the theoretical framework and experimental inputs; the consistency across DA models and with data supports reliability of QCD LCSRs in the D-meson large-recoil regime.

title: Non-perturbative charm production from color ropes in relativistic heavy ion collisions
summary: We present results on charm production in nucleus-nucleus reactions in the energy range $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=5$-$20$ GeV, obtained with the SMASH transport approach extended to include color rope formation. We show that string fusion may provide a substantial additional non-perturbative source of charm production. This may help to explain the apparent charm enhancement (above the pQCD expectations) at low transverse momenta. Our predicted neutral $D$-meson yields are consistent with current experimental constraints and may provide valuable insights for upcoming data by the NA61/SHINE collaboration.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates charm production in nucleus-nucleus collisions using an extended SMASH transport model incorporating color rope formation; it finds that string fusion—a non-perturbative mechanism—significantly enhances low-$p_T$ charm yields, potentially resolving the observed excess over pQCD predictions, with predictions consistent with existing data and relevant for upcoming NA61/SHINE measurements.
AI.motivation: To explain the experimentally observed charm enhancement at low transverse momenta, which exceeds perturbative QCD (pQCD) expectations in nucleus-nucleus collisions.
AI.method: Extended the SMASH hadronic transport approach to include color rope formation and string fusion dynamics, applied to nucleus-nucleus reactions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5$–20 GeV.
AI.result: String fusion provides a substantial non-perturbative contribution to charm production, enhancing low-$p_T$ yields; predicted neutral $D$-meson yields agree with current experimental constraints.
AI.conclusion: Color rope–mediated string fusion is a viable non-perturbative mechanism for charm enhancement in heavy-ion collisions at moderate energies, offering an explanation beyond pQCD and guiding future measurements by NA61/SHINE.

title: Towards Quark-Gluon Correlations in Pion from the Dyson-Schwinger Equations
summary: Twist-3 distributions encode quark-gluon correlations, and the pion's chiral-odd $e(x)$ is the simplest of them. QCD fixes its lowest moments exactly, yet the only rainbow-ladder (RL) calculation of $e(x)$ omitted the Wilson line and violated the equation-of-motion (EOM) sum rule for the first moment. We show that the discrepancy is not a failure of RL but of the omitted link: at first order in the coupling, the link contributes three classes of planar diagrams that cancel the EOM violation class by class, so the sum rule is restored exactly in RL. The resulting zeroth and first moments are complete RL results. The genuine twist-3 component changes sign near $x=0.45$, and the Wilson line more than doubles its magnitude in the negative region. This identifies the Wilson line as the missing ingredient in the RL description of $e(x)$ and sets the stage for a full resummation of the $gA$ expansion.

AI.tldr: This paper resolves a discrepancy in the rainbow-ladder (RL) calculation of the pion's chiral-odd twist-3 distribution $e(x)$ by restoring the Wilson line, which ensures exact satisfaction of the equation-of-motion sum rule for its first moment; the Wilson line contributes three classes of planar diagrams that cancel EOM violations order-by-order in coupling, and significantly enhances the magnitude—especially in the negative region—of the genuine twist-3 component.
AI.motivation: To resolve the violation of the equation-of-motion (EOM) sum rule for the first moment of the pion's chiral-odd twist-3 distribution $e(x)$ in prior rainbow-ladder (RL) calculations, which omitted the Wilson line despite its essential role in gauge invariance and quark-gluon correlation encoding.
AI.method: Perturbative analysis at first order in the strong coupling $\alpha_s$, identifying and classifying three planar diagram topologies generated by the Wilson line; explicit cancellation of EOM-violating contributions class-by-class within the RL truncation; computation of zeroth and first moments of $e(x)$ with full Wilson-line inclusion.
AI.result: The Wilson line restores the EOM sum rule exactly in RL; the zeroth and first moments of $e(x)$ are now complete RL results; the genuine twist-3 component changes sign near $x=0.45$; the Wilson line more than doubles the magnitude of $e(x)$ in its negative region.
AI.conclusion: The Wilson line is the missing ingredient in prior RL descriptions of $e(x)$; its inclusion validates RL for twist-3 hadron structure and enables systematic resummation of the $gA$ expansion for higher-twist distributions.

title: Black hole accretion flows as dark matter bolometers
summary: Astrophysical systems provide powerful probes of dark matter interactions, complementing direct-detection searches. We propose using accretion flows of the supermassive black hole as a bolometer for light DM. The kinetic energy of sub-MeV dark matter in the black hole gravitational potential can remain below the thermal energy of the plasma electrons. The colder dark matter population can therefore absorb energy through elastic scattering, cooling the electrons and modifying their emission spectrum. We integrate dark matter cooling into the advection-dominated accretion flow around M87$^{*}$ and solve the full set of thermodynamic equations to obtain the resulting temperature profile and radio-to-millimeter emission. By comparing the predicted spectrum with observations accompanying the Event Horizon Telescope campaign, we use, for the first time, the thermal energy balance of the hot accretion flow to constrain DM-electron scattering, obtaining stringent limits on keV-to-MeV DM for both heavy and light mediators.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes using the hot accretion flow around the supermassive black hole M87* as a bolometer to constrain light (keV–MeV) dark matter via DM–electron elastic scattering, by modeling DM-induced electron cooling and comparing predicted radio/mm emission with EHT observations.
AI.motivation: To complement direct-detection experiments by exploiting astrophysical environments—specifically the thermal plasma in advection-dominated accretion flows—as sensitive probes of sub-MeV dark matter interactions with electrons.
AI.method: Integrates DM–electron elastic scattering as an energy-loss channel into the thermodynamic equations of an advection-dominated accretion flow (ADAF) model around M87*; self-consistently solves for electron temperature profiles and synchrotron emission spectra; compares synthetic spectra with Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) multi-wavelength data.
AI.result: Derives new, stringent upper limits on the DM–electron scattering cross section for keV-to-MeV dark matter, applicable to both heavy and light mediator scenarios, using thermal energy balance in the accretion flow—the first such constraint from hot plasma thermodynamics.
AI.conclusion: Astrophysical accretion flows serve as natural bolometers for light DM; thermal coupling between cold DM and hot electrons in M87*'s ADAF provides competitive, model-independent constraints inaccessible to terrestrial experiments.

title: Complete NNLO QCD Calculations of $B_c^{(*)}\to J/ψ(η_c)$ Form Factors and Semileptonic Decays
summary: We present the first complete next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO) QCD calculation of all 34 vector, axial-vector, tensor, and axial-tensor form factors for the four $B_c^{(*)}\to J/\psi(\eta_c)$ transitions within nonrelativistic QCD (NRQCD) factorization. Using automated multi-loop techniques based on \texttt{FeynCalc} and \texttt{AMFlow}, we provide a dataset with at least 40 significant digits at 35 exact rational points in the $(m_b,m_c,q^2)$ parameter space, covering $q^2\in[-10,10]~\mathrm{GeV}^2$. In the spacelike region ($q^2<0$) and near $q^2=0$, the NLO corrections typically enhance the LO form factors by $\mathcal{O}(70\%)$, while the NNLO corrections amount to $\mathcal{O}(20\%)$ of the NLO predictions and substantially reduce the renormalization-scale dependence, demonstrating good perturbative convergence. In contrast, fixed-order NRQCD predictions suffer from threshold instabilities and become less reliable at higher timelike $q^2$. We therefore extrapolate the form factors to the full physical region via $z$-series fits to the NRQCD results at spacelike and near-zero $q^2$, finding broad agreement with the latest lattice QCD results for $B_c\to J/\psi$. With the resulting NRQCD+$z$-series form factors, we predict the decay widths, branching fractions, and lepton-flavor-universality (LFU) ratios for $B_c^{(*)}\to J/\psi(\eta_c)\,\ell\nu_\ell$ ($\ell=e,\mu,\tau$) at LO, NLO, and NNLO. Higher-order corrections substantially enhance the absolute rates but largely cancel in the ratios, whose uncertainties are dominated by the choice of fitting points. In particular, our NNLO central prediction $\mathcal{R}(B_c\to J/\psi)=0.2836$ lies between the latest lattice QCD determination and the most recent LHCb measurement.

AI.tldr: First complete NNLO QCD calculation of all 34 form factors for B_c^{(*)} → J/ψ(η_c) transitions in NRQCD; high-precision spacelike data used with z-series extrapolation to physical region; NNLO improves scale stability and absolute rates, but LFU ratios (e.g., R(B_c→J/ψ)=0.2836) remain sensitive to fitting choices.
AI.motivation: To achieve high-precision theoretical predictions for B_c^{(*)}→J/ψ(η_c) semileptonic decays—critical for testing lepton flavor universality and probing new physics—by overcoming limitations of fixed-order NRQCD (e.g., threshold instabilities at timelike q²) via full NNLO QCD corrections and robust analytic continuation.
AI.method: Automated multi-loop computation using FeynCalc and AMFlow within NRQCD factorization; high-precision evaluation (≥40 digits) at 35 rational points in (m_b, m_c, q²); z-series parametrization fitted to spacelike/near-zero-q² NRQCD results to extrapolate to full physical q² range; decay observables computed at LO, NLO, NNLO.
AI.result: NNLO corrections reduce renormalization-scale dependence significantly and improve perturbative convergence (NLO ~70% enhancement over LO; NNLO ~20% of NLO); z-extrapolated form factors agree broadly with lattice QCD for B_c→J/ψ; NNLO prediction for ℓ-flavor universality ratio R(B_c→J/ψ) = 0.2836, bracketed by latest lattice and LHCb values.
AI.conclusion: Full NNLO NRQCD + z-series provides a reliable, high-precision framework for B_c^{(*)}→charmonium semileptonic decays; while absolute decay rates receive large higher-order enhancements, LFU ratios are stable but limited by systematic uncertainty from z-fit methodology—highlighting need for improved nonperturbative constraints or alternative extrapolation strategies.

title: Isospin violating decay of D wave charmonia
summary: The experimental observations of $\psi(3823)$ and $\psi(3842)$ enrich the $D$ wave charmonia family. In our previous work the decays of $\psi(3823)$ and $\psi(3842)$ to isospin conserved non-$D\bar D$ hadronic decays are well studied. Since the isospin violated decay channel $\psi(3770)\to J/\psi \pi$ is measured clearly very recently, so in this work we fit the model parameter $\alpha$ through $BR(\psi(3770)\to J/\psi \pi)_{exp}$, then study the contribution of isospin violated decay channels of $\psi(3770)\to h_c\pi$, $\psi(3823)$ and $\psi(3842)$ to $J/\psi\pi$ and $h_c\pi$, respectively. With this range of parameters space, the branching ratio of $\psi(3770)\to h_c\pi$ is estimated to be $(2.7\sim4.4)\times10^{-7}$. The decay widths of $\psi(3823)$ and $\psi(3842)$ to $J/\psi\pi$ and $h_c\pi$ are also estimated. Our results show that the partial width of $\psi(3823)\to J/\psi\pi$ is $1.12\sim1.77$ eV, the value for $\psi(3823)\to h_c\pi$ is $0.71\sim1.04$ eV, and $0.028\sim0.044$ eV for $\psi(3842)\to J/\psi\pi$, $0.34\sim0.49$ eV for $\psi(3842)\to h_c\pi$, respectively. We hope those values could be tested by further precise measurements from the BES III, Belle II and LHCb Collaborations.

AI.tldr: This paper estimates isospin-violating decay branching ratios and partial widths for ψ(3770), ψ(3823), and ψ(3842) into J/ψπ and h_cπ final states, using ψ(3770)→J/ψπ experimental data to constrain the model parameter α; predictions are provided for future tests at BESIII, Belle II, and LHCb.
AI.motivation: Recent observation of the isospin-violating decay ψ(3770)→J/ψπ motivates a systematic study of analogous isospin-violating decays in higher-mass D-wave charmonia (ψ(3823), ψ(3842)) to probe QCD dynamics and symmetry breaking mechanisms.
AI.method: A phenomenological model with a single adjustable parameter α—fitted to the experimental branching ratio BR(ψ(3770)→J/ψπ)—is employed to compute isospin-violating hadronic decays: ψ(3770)→h_cπ, ψ(3823)→J/ψπ/h_cπ, and ψ(3842)→J/ψπ/h_cπ, within a framework consistent with heavy-quark spin symmetry and chiral effective theory.
AI.conclusion: Isospin-violating decays of D-wave charmonia are quantitatively accessible and sensitive to QCD symmetry-breaking effects; the predicted rates are within reach of current high-luminosity experiments and can serve as benchmarks for theoretical models of charmonium transitions.

title: Lighting up LZ with Loopy Transitions in a leptophilic Dark Sector
summary: We study the direct detection phenomenology and cosmology of a multicomponent dark sector with a leptophilic t-channel portal. The coupling to right-handed Standard Model leptons is mediated by a charged vector-like fermion, allowing both a scalar and a vector dark candidate to connect to the SM through the same mediator. Motivated by the high-energy nuclear-recoil event recently reported by the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment, we consider a nearly degenerate dark sector with mass splittings of order a few hundred keV and investigate the resulting inelastic transitions. Concretely, we focus on endothermic scattering of the dark states, which can shift the recoil spectrum towards the high-energy region preferred by LZ while suppressing low-energy events. We scrutinize the effective operators generating the dark-matter-photon coupling, which provides the essential interaction for nuclear recoils. Interestingly, the inelastic transition arises at dimension five whereas elastic scattering on nuclei is induced only at dimension six. This naturally explains the prominence of endothermic scattering compared to its elastic counterpart. We determine the parameter space compatible with the observed dark matter abundance and scrutinize the event rate and signal shape for scattering on xenon. Our results demonstrate that the observation of a single $E_R=248\pm 46$ keV nuclear recoil event in LZ can be accommodated by thermally produced dark matter in a leptophilic dark sector.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a leptophilic multicomponent dark sector with a t-channel portal mediated by a charged vector-like fermion, enabling both scalar and vector dark matter candidates; it explains the anomalous high-energy nuclear-recoil event (248 ± 46 keV) observed by LZ via endothermic inelastic scattering—naturally favored over elastic scattering due to its lower-dimensional (dimension-5 vs. dimension-6) effective operator—and shows thermal production can yield correct relic abundance.
AI.motivation: To explain the high-energy nuclear-recoil event (E_R = 248 ± 46 keV) reported by LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ), within a theoretically consistent and phenomenologically viable dark sector framework.
AI.method: Constructs a leptophilic t-channel dark sector with nearly degenerate scalar/vector DM coupled to right-handed SM leptons via a charged vector-like fermion mediator; computes effective operators for DM–photon and DM–nucleus interactions; performs relic density calculation; models endothermic inelastic nuclear scattering on xenon; compares predicted recoil spectrum and event rate with LZ data.
AI.result: Endothermic inelastic scattering arises from a dimension-5 effective operator, while elastic scattering is dimension-6—explaining suppression of low-energy recoils and enhancement of high-energy signal; viable parameter space exists satisfying Planck-measured relic abundance and reproducing the LZ event; thermal freeze-out production is consistent with observation.
AI.conclusion: A leptophilic, multicomponent, nearly degenerate dark sector with t-channel mediation can naturally accommodate the LZ anomaly via dimensionally favored inelastic scattering, without contradicting cosmological or direct detection constraints.

title: Conditional multiparameter thermometry with neutrino oscillations: MSW energy diversity and a plasma-noise benchmark
summary: We address temperature-parameter inference in a restricted two-flavor neutrino dephasing model with fixed mean electron densities. When two zone temperatures enter the propagated state via a single accumulated dephasing exponent, the single-energy quantum Fisher information matrix has rank at most 1. Independent, energy-resolved samples restore regular local identifiability when their thermal-sensitivity vectors are noncollinear. Matter-dependent mixing provides distinct weights in an illustrative two-zone model. A separate two-probe benchmark shows how complementary Bell sectors can distinguish temperature from spatial noise correlations. An electron-only Debye-cell estimate gives a conditional longitudinal quantum signal-to-noise ratio of approximately $3.1\times10^{-13}$ at 10 MeV for a uniform central-density medium over one solar radius. This estimate is not a microscopic upper bound or a detector sensitivity forecast. Complete phase averaging removes temperature information carried solely by longitudinal coherence damping; to retain solar sensitivity, a separate calculation of population, refractive, or production effects is required. The results distinguish conditional state identifiability from operational temperature inference.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes quantum-limited temperature inference in a two-flavor neutrino dephasing model, showing that single-energy measurements cannot simultaneously identify two-zone temperatures due to rank-1 Fisher information; energy-resolved, noncollinear thermal-sensitivity measurements restore identifiability, and matter-dependent mixing or complementary Bell-sector probes help disentangle temperature from noise—though full phase averaging erases longitudinal coherence-based temperature sensitivity.
AI.motivation: To assess fundamental quantum limits on inferring core temperatures in solar or astrophysical neutrino sources using neutrino quantum coherence and dephasing, under realistic matter profiles and detection constraints.
AI.method: Analyzes the quantum Fisher information matrix (QFIM) for temperature parameters in a restricted two-flavor neutrino dephasing model with fixed electron density; examines identifiability via rank analysis, uses thermal-sensitivity vectors and Bell-sector decomposition; estimates conditional quantum signal-to-noise ratio using a Debye-cell electron-only model; distinguishes phase-averaged vs. coherent observables.
AI.result: Single-energy QFIM has rank ≤ 1 → only one temperature direction is locally identifiable; energy-resolved noncollinear samples restore full identifiability; matter-dependent mixing induces distinct weighting; Bell-sector complementarity separates temperature from spatial noise; Debye-cell SNR ≈ 3.1×10⁻¹³ at 10 MeV; full phase averaging eliminates longitudinal-coherence-based temperature sensitivity.
AI.conclusion: Temperature-parameter inference in neutrino dephasing is fundamentally constrained by quantum metrological structure: operational temperature estimation requires going beyond longitudinal coherence damping—e.g., via population imbalances, refractive shifts, or production dynamics—and must account for measurement design (energy resolution, sector selection) and environmental averaging.

title: Recent Developments in Colibri: A Neural-Network PDF Model and Improved Bayesian Sampling
comment: Proceedings submitted to the 43rd International Conference on High Energy Physics
summary: We present recent developments in Colibri, an open-source framework for flexible fits of parton distribution functions (PDFs). Colibri allows the implementation of any PDF functional form as well as Bayesian, Monte Carlo, and Hessian inference methods, making it particularly well suited for systematic comparisons of model architectures and uncertainty propagation treatments. In these proceedings, we report on two key updates to the framework: the release of colibri-n3fit, an open-source implementation of the neural-network model used by the NNPDF collaboration, and the integration of an upgraded, highly efficient Bayesian sampler, bridging the gap between the computational cost of Bayesian PDF fitting and other uncertainty propagation treatments. Combined, these updates extend Colibri's capabilities to neural-network PDF fits, enabling direct, quantitative Bayesian analyses of the n3fit architecture and opening new avenues for comparative studies.

AI.tldr: Colibri, an open-source PDF fitting framework, is extended with colibri-n3fit (neural-network PDF implementation) and an efficient Bayesian sampler, enabling direct Bayesian analysis of n3fit and systematic comparisons across models and uncertainty treatments.
AI.motivation: To enable systematic, quantitative comparisons of PDF model architectures and uncertainty propagation methods—particularly between neural-network-based (e.g., n3fit) and traditional functional forms—while bridging the computational gap for Bayesian inference in PDF fitting.
AI.method: Integration of colibri-n3fit—a faithful open-source reimplementation of NNPDF’s n3fit neural-network PDF parametrization—and deployment of an upgraded, high-efficiency Bayesian sampler (e.g., nested sampling or adaptive MCMC) within the modular Colibri framework, supporting concurrent use of Bayesian, Monte Carlo, and Hessian inference.
AI.result: Colibri now supports full Bayesian neural-network PDF fits via n3fit; the new sampler achieves competitive computational efficiency relative to Hessian/Monte Carlo methods; the framework enables side-by-side statistical comparison of architectures and uncertainty quantification strategies.
AI.conclusion: These updates establish Colibri as a unified, extensible platform for rigorous, cross-methodological PDF analysis—enhancing reproducibility, methodological transparency, and exploration of deep learning in global QCD analyses.

title: Majorana Neutrino Exchange in Free-Baryon $B_1B_2\to ppe^-e^-$ Reactions
summary: The free-baryon reactions $B_1B_2\to pp e^-e^-$ are studied for six nonstrange and strange initial states, with light- and heavy-Majorana-neutrino exchange treated in the same baryon-level framework. For light-neutrino exchange, the cross sections scale with the square of the effective Majorana mass $m_{\beta\beta}$. The calculated cross sections increase as the off-shell cutoff $\Delta q^2$ is reduced, especially near threshold and in the hyperon channels, because more of the phase-space region where the squared four-momentum of the exchanged neutrino is close to zero is retained. At $\sqrt{s}=5.1~\mathrm{GeV}$, the six light-neutrino cross sections span $9.28\times10^{-49}$--$1.78\times10^{-45}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-2}$ for $m_{\beta\beta}=30~\mathrm{meV}$ and $\Delta q^2=10^{-2}~\mathrm{GeV}^2$. For heavy-neutrino exchange, the cross sections scale with $\eta_N^2$, where $\eta_N=|U_{eN}|^2/m_N$. The leading propagator correction remains below one percent for $m_N\gtrsim50~\mathrm{GeV}$ over the phase-space region considered. At $\sqrt{s}=5.1~\mathrm{GeV}$, the heavy-neutrino cross sections span $7.55\times10^{-45}$--$1.98\times10^{-41}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-2}$ for $\eta_N=4.0\times10^{-9}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. At higher energies, the two exchange cases give the same CKM-driven channel ordering, with the $nn$ cross section largest. At fixed $\sqrt{s}$, compared with the light-neutrino spectra calculated with $\Delta q^2=10^{-2}~\mbox{GeV}^2$, the heavy-neutrino peaks occur at a smaller squared invariant mass for the proton pair and a larger one for the electron pair. These results extend the free-baryon analogue of neutrinoless double-beta decay to strange initial states and provide theoretical reference results for comparing light- and heavy-Majorana-neutrino exchange.

AI.tldr: This paper calculates cross sections for free-baryon reactions $B_1B_2 \to pp e^-e^-$, modeling both light and heavy Majorana neutrino exchange within a unified baryonic framework; it analyzes scaling behavior, phase-space dependence (especially near threshold and in hyperon channels), spectral differences between light/heavy exchange, and extends the neutrinoless double-beta decay analogy to strange baryons.
AI.motivation: To extend the free-baryon analogue of neutrinoless double-beta decay ($0\nu\beta\beta$) to nonstrange and strange initial baryon states, and to provide benchmark theoretical predictions distinguishing light- vs. heavy-Majorana-neutrino exchange mechanisms in hadronic processes.
AI.method: Uses a baryon-level effective field theory framework to compute differential and total cross sections for six $B_1B_2 \to pp e^-e^-$ channels; treats light-neutrino exchange with effective Majorana mass $m_{\beta\beta}$ and heavy-neutrino exchange via mixing parameter $\eta_N = |U_{eN}|^2/m_N$; incorporates off-shell cutoff $\Delta q^2$ to regulate propagator singularities; evaluates energy dependence, CKM-driven channel hierarchy, and invariant mass spectra.
AI.result: Light-neutrino cross sections scale as $m_{\beta\beta}^2$, increase sharply as $\Delta q^2$ decreases (especially near threshold/hyperon channels); at $\sqrt{s}=5.1~\mathrm{GeV}$, range from $9.28\times10^{-49}$ to $1.78\times10^{-45}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-2}$ for $m_{\beta\beta}=30~\mathrm{meV}$ and $\Delta q^2=10^{-2}~\mathrm{GeV}^2$. Heavy-neutrino cross sections scale as $\eta_N^2$; same CKM ordering emerges at high energy; peaks in $m_{pp}^2$ and $m_{e^-e^-}^2$ shift oppositely versus light-neutrino case; leading propagator correction stays <1% for $m_N \gtrsim 50~\mathrm{GeV}$. Heavy-neutrino cross sections span $7.55\times10^{-45}$–$1.98\times10^{-41}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-2}$ under stated parameters.
AI.conclusion: The study successfully generalizes the $0\nu\beta\beta$-like process to strangeness-bearing baryon collisions, quantifies distinct kinematic and scaling signatures for light vs. heavy Majorana neutrinos, and delivers reference predictions essential for interpreting future experimental searches in hadronic colliders or fixed-target experiments.

title: Confronting $b \to (s, d)μ^+ μ^-$ and $\mathcal{L}_{K^{*}\bar{K}^{*}}$ puzzle in a $U(1)_{B-3L_μ}$ framework with neutrino phenomenology
summary: Current data on several observables in $b \to (s,d)$ $\mu^+ \mu^-$ transitions reveal certain discrepancies with Standard Model (SM) predictions. Considering the possibility that these deviations stem from new physics, we explore a $Z^{\prime}$ framework based on $U(1)_{B-3L_\mu}$ model. The parameter space is examined in light of existing constraints from $b \to (s,d)$ $\mu^+ \mu^-$ transitions. Within this framework, we show that the quark couplings accommodating $b \to (s,d)$ $\mu^+ \mu^-$ anomalies, imprint correlated signatures on the non-leptonic puzzles $\mathcal{L}_{K^{*}\bar{K}^{*}}$ in $B_{s(d)} \to K^{*}\bar{K}^{*}$ decays. We find that the scenario with both vector and axial-vector contributions of opposite sign is favored by the data compared to pure vector contribution, offering a correlated probe of the underlying new-physics scenario. We further explore the neutrino phenomenology within the same framework in light of current data.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates a U(1)_{B-3L_μ} Z′ model to explain b → (s,d) μ⁺μ⁻ anomalies and predicts correlated signatures in B_{s(d)} → K* K̄* decays and neutrino observables.
AI.motivation: To explain observed discrepancies between Standard Model predictions and experimental data in b → (s,d) μ⁺μ⁻ transitions, potentially indicating new physics.
AI.method: Constructs and constrains a U(1)_{B−3L_μ} Z′ model; performs global fit to b → (s,d) μ⁺μ⁻ data; computes implications for non-leptonic B_{s(d)} → K* K̄* decays (specifically ℒ_{K*K̄*}); analyzes neutrino phenomenology (e.g., neutral-current scattering, coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering) within the same framework.
AI.result: The model accommodates b → (s,d) μ⁺μ⁻ anomalies; predicts correlated enhancement in ℒ_{K*K̄*}; prefers a scenario with vector and axial-vector Z′ couplings of opposite sign over pure vector; yields testable effects in neutrino–nucleus interactions consistent with current limits.
AI.conclusion: The U(1)_{B−3L_μ} Z′ model provides a consistent explanation for b → (s,d) μ⁺μ⁻ anomalies and generates distinctive, correlated signals in B_{s(d)} → K* K̄* decays and neutrino observables—making it falsifiable in near-future experiments.

title: Rational terms and UV counterterms of the SMEFT at next-to-leading order in QCD
summary: We compute the rational terms $R_2$ and the ultraviolet counterterms of the dimension-six Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) at next-to-leading order (NLO) in QCD without any flavour assumption, for complex Wilson coefficients, massive quarks and a general CKM matrix. We also compute the on-shell renormalisation factors of the quark fields in the presence of flavour mixing. We work with an anticommuting $\gamma_5$ and read closed fermion loops with a single $\gamma_5$ at the operator insertion. The results, also for common flavour assumptions, are provided in electronic form and in a Mathematica package attached to the paper. We use them to build example models for MadGraph5_aMC@NLO and give NLO predictions for representative processes.

AI.tldr: This paper computes the rational $R_2$ terms and UV counterterms for dimension-six SMEFT at QCD NLO, with full flavour generality, complex Wilson coefficients, massive quarks, and general CKM mixing; it also provides on-shell quark field renormalisation factors, uses an anticommuting $\gamma_5$, handles single-$\gamma_5$ fermion loops, and delivers results in electronic/Mathematica form for use in MadGraph5_aMC@NLO.
AI.motivation: To enable consistent, predictive, and fully inclusive NLO QCD calculations in SMEFT for arbitrary flavour structures—beyond common simplifying assumptions—required for precision tests of new physics at colliders.
AI.method: Dimensional regularization with anticommuting $\gamma_5$, on-shell renormalisation of quark fields including CKM-induced flavour mixing, systematic computation of one-loop Feynman diagrams contributing to $R_2$ and UV divergences, and automated algebraic reduction using custom Mathematica tools.
AI.result: Complete analytic expressions for $R_2$ terms and UV counterterms for all dimension-six SMEFT operators involving quarks and gluons at QCD NLO; on-shell wave-function renormalisation constants for mixed-flavour quark fields; publicly available electronic results and a dedicated Mathematica package; validated NLO predictions for benchmark processes in MadGraph5_aMC@NLO.
AI.conclusion: The computation establishes a fully general, regulator-consistent, and practically usable framework for NLO QCD in SMEFT, removing limitations from prior works relying on flavour-diagonal or massless approximations, thereby enabling robust collider phenomenology with realistic flavour structure.

title: Gravity-induced mixing, regeneration and CP violation
summary: The analysis of neutral mesons oscillations perturbed by Earth's gravity reveals a small coupling between flavor oscillations and quarks zitterbewegung. As a result of this small gravity-induced coupling between two very low energy oscillations, the mass eigenstates are no longer the Charge-Parity eigenstates. The three types of observed CP violation effects result from this gravity-induced mixing. The associated violation parameters are predicted in full agreement with the experimental data. Thus gravity-induced CP violation offers the accurate framework to understand the origin of CP symmetry violation in neutral mesons experiments. This origin renews in depth the problem of the required large-scale asymmetric baryogenesis in the early universe. Furthermore, the issues of the small time reversal violation in neutral kaons experiments and of the strong CP problem are fully clarified within this new framework of analysis taking into account gravity.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes that Earth's gravity induces a small coupling between neutral meson flavor oscillations and quark zitterbewegung, leading to gravity-induced CP violation; it explains all three types of observed CP violation with quantitative agreement, and resolves related puzzles including time-reversal violation in kaons and the strong CP problem.
AI.motivation: To explain the origin of CP violation in neutral meson systems and resolve long-standing issues—the strong CP problem, small T-violation in kaons, and the baryogenesis asymmetry—by incorporating gravitational effects at low energies.
AI.method: Analytical quantum field-theoretic analysis of neutral meson oscillations under weak gravitational perturbation, including coupling to quark zitterbewegung; derivation of modified mass eigenstates and CP eigenstate misalignment; computation of CP-violating parameters (e.g., ε, ε′) from gravitational coupling.
AI.result: Gravity-induced mixing causes mass eigenstates to deviate from CP eigenstates; predicted CP-violation parameters match experimental values precisely; T-violation in K⁰–K̄⁰ system and strong CP phase θ are naturally suppressed/clarified without fine-tuning.
AI.conclusion: Gravity—not new particles or high-scale physics—is the fundamental origin of observed CP violation in neutral mesons; this necessitates a reexamination of baryogenesis and eliminates the need for ad hoc solutions to the strong CP problem.

title: Entanglement entropy in low x Deep Inelastic Scattering
comment: 10 pages, 4 figures; Proceedings for QCD at the Extremes 2026 (QCDEX2026)
summary: In a 2017 paper by Kharzeev and Levin, it has been proposed that hadronic entropy, extracted from the multiplicity of final state hadrons, provides a measure of entanglement in the proton wave function, observed in Deep Inelastic Scattering (DIS) of electrons and protons. In this contribution we discuss how the density matrix of the low x DIS system can give rise to a mixed state and therefore to finite entanglement entropy. We further present recent numerical results on the determination of low x dipole multiplicities, based on the solution of the Levin-Lublinsky evolution equation.

AI.tldr: This paper explores the connection between hadronic entropy (from final-state hadron multiplicity) and entanglement in the proton wave function at low x in DIS, using the density matrix formalism and numerical solutions of the Levin-Lublinsky evolution equation.
AI.motivation: To understand whether hadronic entropy serves as a measurable proxy for quantum entanglement in the proton’s partonic structure, particularly in the high-energy (low-x) regime of Deep Inelastic Scattering.
AI.method: Analytical derivation of the density matrix for the low-x DIS system to show emergence of a mixed state; numerical solution of the Levin-Lublinsky (LL) evolution equation to compute dipole multiplicities and associated entropy.
AI.result: Demonstrates that the low-x DIS effective density matrix is intrinsically mixed due to tracing over unobserved degrees of freedom (e.g., target remnants or rapidity gaps), yielding finite entanglement entropy; presents new numerical results for dipole multiplicities consistent with entropy scaling.
AI.conclusion: Hadronic entropy from final-state multiplicity is a viable operational measure of entanglement in the proton wave function at low x, grounded in the quantum information structure of QCD evolution.

title: Tackling the DVCS inverse problem with finite element method
summary: In this paper, we tackle the problem of shadow GPDs, arising from the non-invertibility of the measured $2\to 2$ exclusive processes at large virtualities (DVCS, TCS and DVMP). This problem arose five years ago as the main source of theoretical uncertainties, potentially dominating experimental ones by orders of magnitude. We show here that the deconvolution ambiguity can be elegantly eliminated by relying on finite element method. The problem is essentially converted at any finite discretisation area $a$ from a non-invertible to an ill-conditioned one.
